# Progress Tracker — Form-Builder SaaS

**Single source of truth for "where are we right now."** Keep the top three sections
(Current Status · Next Session · the G table) current. Full per-session narrative history
lives in [PROGRESS_ARCHIVE.md](PROGRESS_ARCHIVE.md) and in git — do **not** re-read it to resume.

## Standing Rules

1. **Keep this tracker current** — update "Current Status" + "Next Session" as work completes. Never leave the repo in a state the next session has to reverse-engineer.
2. **One shared design system, no exceptions** — every page (builder, dashboard, inbox, settings, public runtime) uses the same app shell + component library + tokens (plan Main Feature #6 / DSR doc #19). Any exception needs a documented rationale.
3. **Fully styled by default** (confirmed 2026-07-05) — every page ships fully styled from shared components; only pure backend/API increments have no styling work. Don't re-ask "styled vs unstyled?" per increment.
4. **End every session** (confirmed 2026-07-10, **reaffirmed a third time 2026-08-08**) with (a) a save to the MD files changed this session — this tracker's top sections + one dated line in `PROGRESS_ARCHIVE.md`, plus any `docs/**`/ADR/plan actually touched — and (b) a copy-paste "what to prompt next" line. Keep it lean: update the top of this file + append one archive line; don't rewrite the whole history. **The closing chat message is a 3–5 bullet status, then the fenced next-prompt ALONE** (amendment 2026-08-08): the bullets are a scannable header, and the ban from 2026-07-23/07-31 still holds for everything in and around the fenced block — no env caveats, gate results, decisions or lessons in chat, they live here. Never hand off leaving the next session to reverse-engineer state from git.

5. **Build everything buildable — the user's testing NEVER gates development** (confirmed 2026-08-06, and it SUPERSEDES the 2026-08-05 "leave every PR open until the app is testable" instruction). Their words: *"let's focus on all the tasks that can be made by you. I will test the app when it is completely built so it will not delay the development. I don't want any pending tasks to be missed."* So: never defer, park, or leave a PR unmerged because the user cannot verify it yet. Merge into the integration branch on green and keep going. `main` still receives nothing until the ONE final integration PR — that part of the original intent stands. **The only surviving blocker is an input the user alone possesses** (OCR scans; third-party OAuth credentials; a Stripe account; hardware), and even then, build every part that does not need it. A design decision the user has not made is NOT automatically a blocker: propose one, recommend, and proceed unless it is genuinely theirs (pricing, legal, an authorization widening).

   **⛔ AMENDED 2026-08-12 — A HELD ROW IS OUT OF SCOPE, NOT PENDING. STOP SURFACING IT.** The user's words: *"i told you that we will skip all tasks that needs my interaction. so you can focus on all the tasks that you can do by yourself. as long as the task doesnt require the tasks that i told you to put on hold."* Rule 5 already said their testing does not gate building; this closes the other half — **a held row must not be reported, counted, scheduled, or asked about at all.** It stopped being work the moment it was held, and re-enters ONLY on the user's explicit signal.

   **THE HELD LIST IS CLOSED AND NAMED** — nothing joins it without the user saying so: the **OCR chain** (H1d → H18a/b → H19a/b) · **all uploading / import features** incl. bulk Excel/CSV (the 2026-08-09 explicit-signal decision) · **payments** (H1c, H20, Cashier/Stripe-Tax) · **Track B** deployment · **GDPR / legal / pricing** calls.

   **THE FAILURE MODE IS REPORTING, NOT BUILDING** — building held rows had already stopped; surfacing them had not. Four consequences. **(1) Progress percentages and pending-task counts are computed over BUILDABLE scope only** — a held row is not a denominator. State held rows separately and briefly, or omit them; never as "blocked on you", never as the reason a phase is incomplete. The 2026-08-12 status report is the worked example of getting this wrong: it opened Phase 3 with "cannot be finished without you" — true and useless — while burying H16b/H16c, the two rows that *can* be finished. **(2) Never present a held row as the next step, and never re-derive its blocker for the user** — they know; they are the one who held it. **(3) A held row never blocks its neighbours** — build every non-held row in the queue regardless of where the held one sits in the order. **(4) Do not ask which of two buildable lanes to take** — when a second agent is running, take the lane with NO file overlap and proceed. An `AskUserQuestion` about lane choice was rejected on 2026-08-12 for exactly this; an alignment question is warranted only when both lanes touch the same files.

   **⚠️ AND NEVER IDLE ON A HELD ROW — ADVANCE TO THE NEXT PHASE AUTOMATICALLY (user decision 2026-08-12).** Their words: *"in case nothing is left to do in the phase 3 and i still did not ask to start what i told you to hold, will we start phase 4 already? it should be."* So when the current phase's only remaining rows are held, **start the next phase without asking**; a held row never stalls the queue and never keeps a phase "open". **Phase 4 is not wholly buildable either** — payments was cut *into* it from Phase 3 and is held, and GDPR *tooling* is buildable while the GDPR/legal/pricing *call* is not — so enter Phase 4 on **SSO/SAML, dedicated-DB tenancy, data residency and CRDT sync**, and apply this same rule again inside it. ⚠️ Note the queue order this does NOT change: Phase 3's non-held remainder is only **H16b/H16c**, but JR3–JR5, J3, J4, J5 and the final integration PR are all still non-held work sitting ahead of Phase 4.

   **⚠️ WHEN A SECOND AGENT HAS THE WORKING TREE, MAKE NO EDITS TO IT — INCLUDING THIS FILE.** Both sessions share one checkout, so a tracker write lands on whatever branch the other agent has checked out, and a branch switch yanks the tree out from under them mid-run. Use `git worktree add --detach <scratch> origin/phase1-completion`, commit there, and `git push origin HEAD:phase1-completion` — which is how this very amendment was landed. **Say plainly in the hand-off that the tracker was not updated** if it could not be.

   **⛔ AMENDMENT 2026-08-17 — THE NEXT-PROMPT IS OWED WHEN THE WORK IS DONE, NOT WHEN THE USER ASKS A QUESTION. DO NOT PAUSE MID-ROW. APPLIES TO BOTH LANES.** The user's words: *"why did we pause if its not done? … if we are done. please provide the next prompt unless, nothing is left in the pipeline for the specific lanes. this is applicable for both lanes."*

   **A QUESTION IS NOT A STOP INSTRUCTION.** Asked *"are we done here?"* with half a row unbuilt, the correct answer is **"no, X remains"** — and then **keep building.** Handing back a fenced next-prompt at that moment reads as *"this is finished"*, which is the one thing it must never say. That is exactly what happened on 2026-08-17: J4c1 had merged, J4c2 was untouched, and the session closed out as if the row were complete.

   **THREE CONSEQUENCES.** **(a) Only close out when the ROW is genuinely complete** — a split row (J4a/J4b/J4c, J4c1/J4c2, J3a/J3b/J3c) is not done until every half has merged. **(b) When a lane's queue empties, Rule 7(f) governs and it does not say "stop"** — claim the unassigned remainder, and only the lane that empties LAST recommends the final integration PR. **(c) If a pause is genuinely needed** — a background gate, a CI run, a container build — **say so in chat in one line using the word *wait*, per Rule 6**, and then resume without being asked. Silence during a long run is indistinguishable from being finished, which is the failure this amendment and Rule 6 both exist to prevent.

6. **Signal every wait — never end a message ambiguous** (added 2026-08-08, the in-session half of Rule 4's hand-off contract). Before ANY pause — a background agent, the Pest/Vitest/PHPStan gate suites, `npm ci`, a container build, waiting on a CI run — **say so in one line first**: what is running, roughly how long, and that nothing is needed from the user yet. Use the word *wait* explicitly; "let me check…" is not a signal. **Say "done" when it returns**, before the results. **Mark 👉 your turn** when the turn is genuinely theirs. The user's words (2026-08-08): *"everytime you pause, make sure to inform me that I need to wait and you are working on something in the background so I won't be asking if we are waiting for something and ask you if we can move forward to the next session… I must be notified because I cannot read everything you say."* Silence during a long run is indistinguishable from being finished — this rule exists so "am I waiting, or is Claude working?" is never answerable only by guessing. Chat text only; the user chose this over a desktop/sound alert, so there is no hook to maintain.

7. **TWO AGENTS = TWO WORKTREES, ONE DATABASE** (added 2026-08-12, user decision). Running two sessions in parallel is supported and encouraged, but **only** under this protocol. It supersedes Rule 5's "make no edits while another agent has the tree", which was the emergency workaround for having no protocol at all.

   **(a) ONE WORKTREE PER AGENT — NEVER TWO SESSIONS IN ONE CHECKOUT.** A checkout has exactly one HEAD, so a `git checkout` in one session silently relocates or clobbers the other's uncommitted work. Lane A keeps `c:\laragon\www\dev_formbuilder_app`; lane B gets its own directory sharing the same `.git`:
   `git worktree add ../fb-lane-b -b <branch> origin/main`
   Git refuses to check out one branch in two worktrees — that is a guardrail, not an obstacle. Remove a finished lane with `git worktree remove ../fb-lane-b`.

   ✅ **REWRITTEN 2026-08-18 — `main` IS THE TRUNK AND `phase1-completion` IS RETIRED.** PR #179 (`52754ed`) merged the integration branch into `main`, the two trees are identical, and the user's decision the same day is that **new work branches from `origin/main` and PRs into `main`, self-merged on 6/6 green**. `phase1-completion` is no longer checked out in any worktree, so the 2026-08-15 note that it *“is checked out in `fb-lane-b`, so the other lane cannot check it out at all”* is **spent** — it described a lock that no longer exists. ⚠️ **WHAT SURVIVES IT IS THE HALF THAT WAS NEVER ABOUT THAT BRANCH: ALWAYS `git fetch` AND BRANCH FROM `origin/main`, NEVER FROM LOCAL `HEAD`.** Each worktree still sits on whatever it last shipped (Lane A on `j8-tracker`, Lane B on its last increment), so a branch cut from local `HEAD` is cut from a stale base and inherits none of what the other lane has since fixed. That is a property of two worktrees, not of one integration branch, and it outlives the branch that taught it.

   **(b) ASSIGN LANES BY SUBSYSTEM, NOT BY ROW.** Two rows from the same queue usually touch the same files; two *subsystems* do not. Both PR into `phase1-completion`; **never PR one lane into the other.**

   **⚠️ AMENDED 2026-08-15 — THE BOUNDARY LIVES HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE, BECAUSE TWO COPIES OF IT DRIFTED APART AND NEITHER LANE COULD SEE IT.** Each lane's next-prompt had been *restating* its own version of the split, and by 2026-08-15 the two statements **contradicted each other**: Lane A's conceded five named subtrees to Lane B, while Lane B's claimed **all** of `app/Services/`, **all** of `app/Support/` and **all** of `config/`. Lane A's very next row (J4b) edits `app/Support/Navigation/CrumbTrail.php`, which is Lane A's under one map and a trespass under the other — **and both lanes would have been reading their own map correctly.** That is the ADR-0017 collision shape exactly (each lane checked, each was right, the artefact still collided), so the fix is the same one: **one authority, referenced rather than copied.** A next-prompt may now say only *"the boundary is Standing Rule 7(b)"* — **a next-prompt that restates the table is the defect, not a convenience.**

   | LANE B owns | LANE A owns | NEITHER — claim in this file FIRST |
   |---|---|---|
   | `app/Services/{Sso,Tenancy,Connectors}/` | `packages/design-system/` | `docs/` (except each lane's own ADR) |
   | `app/Support/{Sso,Tenancy,Connectors}/` | `resources/js/{Pages,Layouts,components/shell}/` | `PROGRESS.md` — own block only, per (d) |
   | `config/`, `scripts/`, `app/Http/Middleware/` | `app/Support/Navigation/` | `openapi.json`, `ci.yml`, `phpunit.xml` |
   | `app/Http/Controllers/Tenant/Sso/` | controller wiring for Lane A's OWN pages | ADR numbers, migration prefixes — see (g) |
   | `resources/public-runtime/` (CRDT row) | `MEMORY.md` — Lane A only; Lane B never writes memory | `tests/e2e/` — grep it before ANY selector change |

   **THE RULE THAT MAKES THE TABLE HOLD: `app/Services/` AND `app/Support/` ARE NOT WHOLESALE LANE B'S.** Lane B owns the three named subtrees under each; everything else beneath them is unclaimed and taken per-row. `app/Support/Navigation/` is Lane A's on the merits — **Lane A wrote `CrumbTrail` in J2d** when trail resolution moved server-side, and no Lane B row goes near it. A lane whose row needs PHP outside its column does not stop: it claims it per the paragraph below.

   **`resources/public-runtime/` GOES TO LANE B FOR THE CRDT-SYNC ROW** (user decision 2026-08-15) — 19 files (`sw.ts`, `outbox.ts`, `useSyncOutbox.ts`, `SubmissionOutbox.vue`, `SyncStatus.vue` + five test files) that a CRDT rewrite lands in by definition; splitting one offline-sync rewrite across two agents costs more than one agent crossing a line. ⚠️ **THE COST IS STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED: that directory is one of the three chunks Lane A's Vitest gate sums**, so Lane A's **110 files / 1,883 tests** baseline MOVES when CRDT lands. Lane A re-measures after it; it does not assume.

   **(c) ⚠️ THE DATABASE IS THE ONE THING WORKTREES DO NOT DUPLICATE, AND IT IS DESTRUCTIVE.** There is exactly one `dev_formbuilder_app-postgres-1` and one `dev_formbuilder_app-app-1` (verified 2026-08-12). Pest runs `migrate:fresh`, which **DROPS THE SCHEMA** — so two concurrent Pest runs mean one silently wipes the other mid-run, surfacing as bizarre irreproducible failures that read as product bugs. **Gate runs must be serialized.** Before any Pest run, check and wait if it returns non-zero:
   `docker exec dev_formbuilder_app-app-1 sh -c "ps -eo args | grep '[p]est' | wc -l"`
   (Use `wc -l`, not `grep -c` — `grep -c` exits 1 on zero matches and reads as a command failure.) Same single-instance constraint applies to `npm run dev` on port 5173 and to the seeded dev data.

   **✅ AMENDED 2026-08-12 — SERIALIZATION IS RETIRED, BECAUSE THE PREMISE ABOVE IS NO LONGER TRUE. The paragraph is kept because it is right about the DANGER and only wrong about the topology.** "The database is the one thing worktrees do not duplicate" was a statement about how the stack happened to be run, not about worktrees — and a worktree can carry its own compose stack. **Lane B now does**: an UNTRACKED `docker-compose.override.yml` in `c:\laragon\www\fb-lane-b` sets `name: fb-lane-b`, so Compose derives `fb-lane-b-*` containers, an `fb-lane-b_default` network on which the other stack is unreachable by service name, and a separate `fb-lane-b_pgdata` volume. Host ports are remapped app **8081** · postgres **5433** · redis **6380** · vite **5174** · mailpit **1026/8026**; verified free before use, and every published port carries the `!override` tag because **`ports:` merges by APPEND** — without it the second stack inherits 8080/5432/6379/1025/8025/5173 as well and collides on all six.

   **WHAT MAKES THE TEST DATABASE FOLLOW AUTOMATICALLY, AND IT IS ONE LINE THAT WAS ALREADY THERE.** `phpunit.xml` pins `DB_DATABASE=meridian_testing` but says nothing about `DB_HOST`, which falls through to `.env`'s **service name** `postgres`. A service name resolves on the calling container's OWN network, so `meridian_testing` inside `fb-lane-b-app-1` IS `fb-lane-b-postgres-1`'s copy. `migrate:fresh` can only drop the schema of the lane that ran it — **structurally, not by convention**. The same indirection puts the seeded dev data and `npm run dev` (5174, moved INSIDE the container too, or `public/hot` would point the browser at the other lane's Vite) on the same footing.

   **MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED (2026-08-12).** Lane A's dev database read `tenants=2 users=10 forms=7 submissions=518` before and after a full `migrate:fresh --seed` in Lane B — identical — while Lane B's own copy came up independently at `users=9 submissions=534`. `tests/Feature/Connectors` then ran to **153 passed / 593 assertions** entirely inside `fb-lane-b-app-1`. A fresh `pgdata` volume also re-runs `docker/postgres/init/*.sql`, so the three RLS roles, `meridian_testing` and PostGIS arrive for free — **keep that bind mount** or every migration fails on a missing `meridian_app`.

   **THE PROBE STAYS, SCOPED.** Two agents sharing ONE stack is still the destructive case, and that is what the `ps -eo args` check is for — run it against whichever container you are about to test in. What is retired is the requirement to serialize ACROSS lanes. **Both files are untracked and gitignored by name**: `.gitignore:41` ignores `docker-compose.override.yml` and `.gitignore:3` ignores `.env` — and note `.gitignore:3` is the literal `.env`, **not** `.env*`, so `.env.lane-b`, `docker-compose.lane-b.yml` and `compose.lane-b.yml` are all committable and must not be used for this. Two costs, stated rather than discovered: `composer install` on this bind mount exceeds composer's 300 s process timeout (`-e COMPOSER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT=0`), and a second stack means a second `.env`, so a change to one lane's environment does not reach the other.

   **(d) THE TRACKER AND MEMORY NEED A WRITER DISCIPLINE.** Both lanes will want this file. Conflicts are survivable when the regions differ (Standing Rules vs Current Status auto-merged cleanly on 2026-08-12), so **each lane writes only its own Current Status block** and neither reformats the other's. **Memory is more dangerous than the tracker**: `MEMORY.md` and the files beside it are shared, outside git, and **last-write-wins** — two agents editing one memory file loses one silently. Announce a memory write, or leave memory to one lane.

   **(e) THE HAND-OFF IS PER-LANE, NOT PER-SESSION — RULE 4 BREAKS UNDER PARALLELISM AND THIS IS THE FIX.** Rule 4 says "end every session with a save and a copy-paste next-prompt", written when there was exactly one session; with two lanes both would write *the* next prompt and clobber each other. So: **each lane closes with its own 3–5 bullet status and its own fenced next-prompt**, and writes that prompt to **its own labelled line** in `## Next Session — Resume Here` — `**LANE A NEXT PROMPT →** `Read PROGRESS.md, including Standing Rule 7. You are LANE A (design), in the main working tree on phase1-completion. Your subsystem is packages/design-system/, resources/js/Pages/ and resources/js/Layouts/ — do not edit Lane B's (app/Services/Connectors/, app/Support/Connectors/, config/connectors.php, connector pages). Lane A owns MEMORY.md; Lane B does not write memory. **JR5 IS MERGED — PR #142 (`e02a8ce`), 6/6 with real steps; CI Pest 3637/0 (15,468 assertions; the +22 on 3615 is Lane B's H16c, not JR5, which touches no PHP), E2E 506 passed / 0 failed, Storybook axe 223 across 33 suites (unchanged, deliberately), Vitest 101 files. The LAST JR row, so the Vivid re-skin is COMPLETE.** The builder switches panes on `@container (max-width: 60em)` of its own box; `showBuilderPane()` in tests/e2e/support/navigate.ts is the shared way into a builder pane. **BUILD J3 — the auth & registration vertical.** Branch j3-auth-vertical off phase1-completion, PR into it, self-merge on 6/6 green.    ⚠️ **AND THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE CONTAINS A VERBATIM EXAMPLE OF THE HAND-OFF LINE, WHICH MAKES THIS FILE HOSTILE TO A NAIVE SEARCH-AND-REPLACE — LEARNED BY DOING IT TWICE (2026-08-16).** A script that replaced from the FIRST occurrence of the hand-off marker to the Lane B one deleted **1,086 lines** — the whole of Current Status, the roadmap and the ledger — because the first occurrence is the example a few lines up, not the real line ~1,085 lines below. It merged, because a docs-only change is green by construction and the `grep -c` used to check afterwards returned **1**, which reads as success and is in fact the symptom: there should have been TWO.

   ⚠️ **AND THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS VERY WARNING MADE IT WORSE, WHICH IS WHY THE RULE BELOW IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS.** It advised anchoring on the line start — and *quoted the marker to say so*, at a point where the quote wrapped onto a fresh line. That created a THIRD line-start occurrence, inside the note warning about the first two, so a script following its advice would have deleted the file again. **NAME THE THING, NEVER QUOTE IT** — fifth occurrence in this project, and the only one so far to booby-trap its own remedy.

   **SO: match the hand-off marker only where it begins a line, assert it appears exactly once that way, and — the part that actually saves you — ASSERT THE RESULTING LINE COUNT IS WITHIN A PLAUSIBLE DELTA.** A marker check tells you what you found; only the line count tells you what you destroyed.

   **THE LANE QUEUE IS THE CLAIM, AND A CLAIM IS A COMMIT.** A lane takes the top unclaimed row from its own queue and needs no permission. To take a row from the *other* lane's queue — or from the unassigned remainder — **write the claim into this file and commit it FIRST**, because the commit is the only thing the other lane can see. Never start an unclaimed row on the strength of "the other lane probably isn't on it."

Driven with the provider's real shape, the unfixed adapter wrote `{"records":[{"id":"recNEW0000000001","createdTime":"…","fields":{"Full name":"Ana Reyes","Colour":"b","Submission ID":"sub-1"}}]}` straight into the ledger. The new case asserts a **control** first — that the response genuinely carries the answer — so a clean excerpt afterwards is the adapter's doing and not the stub's. **This is M3's lesson (c) in a second shape: a passing test can be a property of the FIXTURE rather than of the code.**

  🔴 **THE ROW WAS TWO DEFECTS WEARING ONE NAME, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM WAS EVER SILENT.** Reproducing before fixing produced **two different failures** from the same code: with **no** ambient context (a worker's state exactly) the fan-out created **zero rows, threw nothing and logged nothing**; with a **different** ambient tenant it raised **42501**, because the SELECT returned the other tenant's endpoints and the INSERT then stamped the event's `tenant_id`, which RLS rejects. So the mismatch case was **already loud and needed no fix** — the defect is the *unset* case, and the fix is aimed there. Both are now pinned, so narrowing either later fails a test.

  ⚠️⚠️ **VERIFYING THE ROW AGAINST THE CODE FOUND FOUR THINGS — TWENTY-FOUR-FOR-TWENTY-FOUR.** **(1) The row named ONE dispatcher and there are TWO** — `ConnectorEventDispatcher` is the identical shape and is the twin that actually carries every Slack / Sheets / Airtable delivery the row blames on the webhook class, so fixing only the named file would have left the row's own sentence false (user decision 2026-08-19: fix both). **(2) Eight listeners per channel, not four**, in both dispatcher docblocks — I3 added three and I9c a fourth. **(3)** the 42501 finding above. **(4) The fix falsified a sentence repeated in SEVEN listener docblocks**, so the sweep is part of the row rather than tidying.

  ⛔ **THE OBVIOUS IMPLEMENTATION WOULD HAVE MASKED THE NEXT REAL EXCEPTION, AND THAT IS WHY `runFor()` HAS THREE EXITS RATHER THAN A `finally`.** *Apply → work → restore in a `finally`* issues SQL on the way out of a **failure**, where Postgres refuses every further statement on an aborted transaction — the restore throws **25P02** and becomes the exception the caller sees. So: on a **throw**, restore the PHP mirror only (the database has already reverted itself); on a **nested** success re-issue the GUC, because a `SET LOCAL` inside a savepoint **survives its release** and would otherwise hand the rest of the enclosing transaction a tenant it never asked for (the H12a sweep is exactly that); on an **outermost** success the COMMIT has already discarded it, so the mirror is all that is left. Rejected in writing: *assert the precondition and throw* (a loud total outage is still a total outage, and the `ShouldQueue` landmine survives) and *skip the wrapper when the mirror already matches* (the mirror is not a sound proxy for the GUC — that divergence is what `ScopeTenantContextToJob` exists to contain).

  ⚠️⚠️ **THE ADVERSARIAL PASS FOUND A LIVE SECURITY DEFECT AFTER ALL SIX JOBS WERE GREEN — THIRD INCREMENT RUNNING, AND THE MOST SERIOUS YET.** Four independent lenses, every finding handed to a skeptic prompted to REFUTE it: **8 raised, 3 refuted, 5 real**, two of them confirmed by the verifier *running* the mutation rather than reading. (1) **OAuth LOGIN-CSRF: nothing bound the browser that STARTED a sign-in to the one that FINISHED it.** A signed `state` proves *we* minted the token; it says nothing about who holds it. An attacker could obtain an authorization `code` without spending it, send a victim the callback URL, and `Auth::login()` would run **on the attacker's account in the victim's browser** — everything the victim then typed, uploaded or configured landing in an account the attacker controls. The tenant arm was the same attack against the handoff URL, accepted in *any* browser with an attacker-chosen `return_to`. Fixed with one session key (`google.flow_sid`) compared at both hops that create a session; no cross-host cookie and no token-format change are needed because each of those hops is same-host with its own mint, and it compares the flow's own `state_id` rather than merely requiring *some* value. ⚠️ **The connector flow does NOT supply this binding either** — its `uid` claim is for attribution and its callback never sees the tenant session — so this is not a protection J3c2 dropped but one the family never had; **ADR-0009 §D3's "the signed state is the CSRF control" is a claim about PROVENANCE that reads like one about ORIGIN**, and that is what made it easy to miss (RFC 6749 §10.12 asks for the missing half explicitly). (2) **The write-path trim evicted LIVE in-flight sign-ins** — ported faithfully from `SsoAuthFailureRecorder::trim()`, whose table holds finished log rows while this one holds live state, so a rank-only cap let anyone push a member's row past the cap while they sat on Google's consent screen: **unauthenticated denial of *authentication* for a whole workspace**, with the log blaming `state_replayed`. Liveness is now the outer `AND`; stated consequence, the table is capped at N *spent* rows plus whatever the limiter admits in one state TTL. (3) **Two tests were vacuous** — the seat-quota "no orphaned account" case asserted two things that were *unconditionally* false (one hidden by RLS with the GUCs cleared, one on a connection that structurally cannot see the test transaction), so deleting `provision()`'s transaction left all 32 green while every full-workspace sign-in stranded a live account; and the trim case compared two reads of the same surviving rows, a tautology that passed even with the subquery inverted to keep the OLDEST N. (4) Four documents claimed all three routes 404 when unconfigured; only the mint route consults the gate. (5) §7.1 implied `MemberJoined` parity across four doors — there are three, and the silent one is invitation acceptance.

No error, no rollback, no timeout; two runs sat for 26 and 75 minutes before `pg_blocking_pids()` named the application's own connection. **A Pest run that HANGS rather than fails is a lock, not a slow host.** (c) A genuine PHPStan `method.notFound` in the committed seam: `fromSocialiteUser()` was typed against `Contracts\User`, which has no `getRaw()` — it compiled, ran and passed its unit tests (which build a concrete `Two\User`) while being wrong the moment anything checked.

  **⚠️⚠️ THE ZERO-ROW DEFECT WAS SIX ENDPOINTS, NOT ONE, AND THE SIXTH WAS A PERMANENT LOCKOUT.** `config/fortify.php` mounted every Fortify route with no tenancy middleware, so `app.current_user_id` was unset. `users_app_update` is permissive — but **PostgreSQL applies SELECT policies to an UPDATE whose `WHERE` reads a column**, and `users_users_visibility` needs the acting user or an ACTIVE co-tenant, so the row was invisible to its own update: zero rows, no exception, no log line, and `save()` does not inspect the affected-row count. Casualties: `PUT /user/profile-information`, `PUT /user/password`, the four 2FA writes — and **`GET /email/verify/{id}/{hash}`, which the backlog entry never named.** `markEmailAsVerified()` wrote nothing while `save()` still returned `true`, so `Verified` fired and the redirect carried `?verified=1`. With J3a's `verified` gate mounted, **a new registrant could follow a valid link, be told it worked, and be bounced back forever** — their only escape being the correction form that posts to the first broken endpoint. Both doors were the same door.

  **THE FIX IS ONE MIDDLEWARE ON THE GROUP, AND THE ALTERNATIVE COULD NOT HAVE WORKED.** A connection swap would have to be repeated per action and **cannot reach the four vendor-owned 2FA/verification controllers at all**. `priority()` cannot substitute for the line — it reorders what a route already carries and never adds. Safe on the guest routes in the same group, which apply `(null, null)`, the value they already had. ⚠️ Documented boundary: it runs BEFORE the controller, so a write issued after `Auth::login()` in the same request still has no GUC.

  ⚠️ **WHY 3,767 PASSING TESTS NEVER CAUGHT IT — THE HARNESS WAS SUPPLYING THE MISSING GUC.** `enterTenant()` issues `SET LOCAL`; `RefreshDatabase` wraps the test in one transaction; the route had no `terminate()` to clear it. `TwoFactorEnrollmentTest` asserted a complete enrol → confirm → recovery-codes round trip **that wrote nothing in production**. Any regression test for this class of bug must clear the GUC with `TenantContext::applyLocal(null, null)` — `forget()` is session-scoped and **cannot clear an in-transaction SET LOCAL**. Measured before relying on it: a session-scoped `set_config` issued AFTER a `SET LOCAL` **does** take effect, which is what lets the fixed middleware win from inside the transaction.

It is not: `users_visibility`'s first arm is `id = app.current_user_id`, **unconditional**, so a caller whose own membership has been removed or suspended still sees their own `users` row. Leaning on RLS alone would seat them on the ladder as a ghost — ranked, named, and no longer a member. Every *other* member is filtered identically by both mechanisms, which is precisely what makes the caller the only case that can tell them apart. **A test now pins it, and the "expected survivor" became a killed mutant.**

  ⚠️⚠️ **VERIFYING THE ROW AGAINST THE CODE FOUND ITS CENTRAL PREMISE FALSE — TWENTY-FOR-TWENTY, AND THIS IS THE SHARPEST ONE YET BECAUSE THE PREMISE WAS IN THREE DOCUMENTS AT ONCE.** The row, doc #28 §9 and ADR-0020 §D5 all say the backfill replays `audits` *"through the same `PointRule` map"*. **There is no such map, and three of the seven rules are not in that ledger at all:** `TenantMembershipService::invite()` writes **no audit row whatsoever**; `accept()` writes neither a row nor an event, so the `('tenant_users','created')` row covers only the three self-serve doors and misses the commonest one; and `('submission','updated')` is written by **two** services, so `(auditable_type, event)` cannot separate a 3-point review from a 1-point edit. So the backfill reads **`audits` for the five act rules and `tenant_users` for the two membership rules**, and review-vs-edit is discriminated on the **shape** of `new_values` (a review always carries `remarks`; an edit carries flattened `answers.<key>` entries; the redactor replaces values in place and never removes a key, so redaction cannot erase the signal). **Anything matching neither marker is counted as UNMAPPED rather than guessed** — which is what makes a future third writer of that tuple visible instead of silently mis-scored.   🔴 **AND IT UNCOVERED A LIVE DEFECT K1a SHIPPED: AN INVITED MEMBER WHO ACCEPTED EARNED NOTHING.** `MemberJoined` was raised only from the private `attachMember()` — self-registration, SAML and Google. `accept()`, the commonest door of all, raised no event, so an accepted invitation produced no `member.joined` points, **no `welcome` badge** (the one badge whose stated purpose is to keep a brand-new member's achievements surface from being blank), and no notification to the Owner who had sent the invitation. **Fixed rather than filed**, because the alternative is a scoreboard that permanently disagrees with itself: the backfill grants every historical invited member their join points from `joined_at`, and the very next acceptance would grant none.   ⚠️ **THE TWO CHANNELS TAKE OPPOSITE POSTURES ON A MISSING TOKEN, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN, NOT AN INCONSISTENCY.** The **draft** channel fails **CLOSED** — a client that omits the token is refused, because a refused autosave tick costs a retype. **Submit** fails **OPEN on an absent claim**, because a submit can arrive from the offline **outbox**, replayed hours later from a row serialized by an earlier build; refusing that strands a finished response nothing can resubmit, which breaks the offline-first promise this subsystem exists to keep. A present-but-**stale** claim is refused on both. Our client always claims, including offline — the baseline is frozen into the outbox row at enqueue (an un-indexed field, so **no Dexie version bump**, per §3).

  🔴 **THE ACS WAS REPLACING THE BROWSER'S SESSION COOKIE, SO P1c's STEP-UP HOP HAD NEVER WORKED IN A REAL BROWSER. MEASURED AGAINST A RUNNING STACK, NOT REASONED.** Inside `web`, `StartSession` finds no cookie on a cross-site POST, mints a fresh id, and `addCookieToResponse()` emits it **unconditionally** — its only guard is `! is_null(session.driver)`. `curl` against `fb-lane-b` returned `Set-Cookie: meridian-session=<a new, empty session>; path=/` plus a regenerated `XSRF-TOKEN`, host-only and same-path, so a browser **replaces** the member's real cookie and then follows our 302 carrying the empty one. A member completing a step-up therefore arrived with no session, was bounced to `/login` by `auth`, and had lost the session the step-up was being performed for; the regenerated CSRF token would have 419'd their next write. **P1e would have 404'd for everybody** — and, sharpest of all, **the outage and the security refusal share ONE observable**, a 404 at the hop, so an acceptance test would have passed either way. ⚠️ **No test in this repository could see it**: the Pest client never feeds `Set-Cookie` into the next request and `Store::loadSession()` merges onto a memoised store — **the harness models the session as a process global; a browser models it as a cookie.** Fixed by taking the ACS out of the stateful stack entirely, which is what its own docblock had claimed since P1b, and pinned by the one assertion that can see it: a response-header assertion.

  ⚠️ **THE ROW COULD NOT BE BUILT AS NAMED, AND THAT IS THE FINDING — SIX-FOR-SIX ON VERIFYING A ROW AGAINST THE CODE.** "Dedicated-database tenancy" is foreclosed here by two things effort cannot move. **Identity is resolved BEFORE any tenant exists**: Fortify routes `/login` with `domain => null`, and `pgsql_auth` exists precisely because the join-shape RLS on `users` fails closed pre-context — so at the moment of login there is no subdomain and therefore no tenant database to look a person up in. And **three RLS policies subquery a neighbouring table** (`users`→`tenant_users`, `resource_grants`→`forms`/`scope_nodes`, draft-children→`form_versions`), which PostgreSQL cannot express across databases; a policy whose referent is absent does not fail closed, it ERRORS on every SELECT. Production is also one box with one PostgreSQL instance (ADR-0005), so the word would have bought blast-radius containment and not isolation, and **not residency at all** — which is a hosting decision, not a schema one. ADR-0017 decides isolation TIERING with the default unchanged, names **schema-per-tenant in the same instance** as the target, and records that this is not one uncommented line: stock `PostgreSQLSchemaManager` REPLACES `search_path` rather than prepending, dropping `public` and with it the `geometry` type, `users`, `tenants`, `jobs` and the `migrations` table.

Because the rows are generated, the search a reader runs before concluding "nothing consumes this key yet" — `grep dedicated_db` — returns a seeder, a docblock and one negative unit test, and never this surface. `PlanCatalog` compounded it: Enterprise's **seeded, rendered** description read *"SSO, dedicated tenancy, and data residency."* Both corrected and pinned. **This is the P1c "a test pins copy, not truth" lesson recurring one increment later, in a place a test could not have been written because nobody knew the sentence existed.**

Eloquent stamps `updated_at` AFTER the `saving` event that does the encoding, so the copy is always one save behind — measured on the dev database: column `19:54:38`, blob `19:54:11`. `created_at` escaped notice for a year only because it never changes, so its two copies always agreed. **The whitelist alone does not heal an existing row** (the decode loop iterates the keys PRESENT IN `data`, not the non-whitelisted ones), hence migration `2026_08_16_000001`, cast through `jsonb` because the column is `json` and `-` exists only for `jsonb`.

The consequence is why `TenantScopedTables` exists as data rather than as a rule: **any future code reasoning "carries `tenant_id`, therefore RLS is filtering it" reads every tenant's hostnames, custom domains and verification tokens.** Classification is a DECISION (`domains` is unprotected because somebody reasoned about it) and no query separates that from somebody forgetting — so the list holds the reasoning and the drift test holds the drift, in BOTH directions.

Use `container-type: inline-size`. This inverts naive breakpointing and is the single easiest way to build JR4 backwards.

  | directory | `find` / `glob` | HOST iterator | CONTAINER iterator |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `database/migrations` | 91 | **91** | **64** |

  **⚠️ NO COLLISION PROBE — THE RETRY IS AT THE TRANSACTION BOUNDARY, AND THE FIRST DESIGN WAS WRONG.**
  The obvious shape is `FormSlug::suggest()`'s "mint, SELECT, re-mint if taken". It cannot work here, for a
  reason `FormSlug` never faces: both writers create INSIDE `DB::transaction`, so a probe is a TOCTOU read
  that proves nothing about a concurrent inserter, and by the time the index raises 23505 the transaction is
  in ERROR state — re-minting in place is impossible (25P02). A probe's attempts are probes, not inserts.
  `SubmissionPipeline` and `SubmissionDraftService` now retry the whole closure, where a fresh
  `Submission::create()` mints again. The 23505 arms are **ORDERED rather than told apart by constraint
  name** (resolve the client-uuid race first; only an unexplained 23505 is a reference collision), which
  keeps `SavedReportViewService`'s "catch the CODE, never match the driver's message" rule intact.
  ⚠️ The backfill hit the SAME 25P02 wall in its own effect test — correct in production (autocommit),
  broken under any caller holding a transaction — so its chunk UPDATE is wrapped in a nested transaction,
  i.e. a SAVEPOINT.

  **⚠️ THE UNIQUE INDEX IS CREATED BEFORE THE BACKFILL, NOT AFTER.** Postgres treats NULLs as distinct, so
  un-backfilled rows coexist under it and the backfill writes THROUGH the constraint — the database is the
  only authority. The rejected alternative (de-duplicate in a PHP `seen` set, then add the index) puts a
  second authority beside the index and can only be tested PROBABILISTICALLY. **No `deleted_at IS NULL`
  arm**, deliberately: a soft-deleted submission keeps its code reserved forever, because freeing it would
  let a code a respondent wrote down resolve LATER to a different submission — strictly worse than "not
  found". The consequence is recorded in `ReapTenantDraftsJob`, whose `forceDelete()` now frees one too.
  Verified against the real seeded database: **521 pre-existing rows, all 521 backfilled, all distinct**,
  with a clean `up → down → up` round trip.

  identical across a ~49-day window. `MIN_UUID_PREFIX` is gone; `referenceCandidate()` (exact) and

It now points at `/submissions?form_id={id}`, which is safe by measurement rather than by hope — `SubmissionInboxController:39` reads `form_id` as a plain query string with **no `Rule::in`** and the presenter composes it as a bare `where`, so a form with zero responses filters to an empty list instead of 422-ing on the submissions-derived dropdown. **The general fix is `FormTabSetReachabilityTest`**: a `->with()` dataset that issues a REAL request per tab href and requires a success, so no future tab can ship as a dead link. One HTTP request per case, never a loop — the tenant GUC is torn down on the way out (`FormHubGateTest` records it). J2c swaps that one line and the hub's Responses tile follows automatically, because the tile reads its href back off the tab set rather than rebuilding the URL.

  **⚠️ `MdsTabNav` AND `MdsBreadcrumb` RENDERED BARE ANCHORS, SO THE HUB'S OWN NAVIGATION WAS A FULL PAGE LOAD.** The design-system package imports **zero** Inertia by design (Storybook renders it with no router), so J2a's strip and trail were plain `a href` — meaning every tab click tore down the persistent `AppLayout` that `app.ts:23-25` exists to keep mounted, re-initialising the ⌘K palette, the notification poll and the theme. **User decision: both gained an optional `linkComponent` prop defaulting to the string `'a'`**, and the app passes Inertia's `Link`. The package still imports no router, and `TabNav.test.ts` / `Breadcrumb.test.ts` / every story pass **UNEDITED** — which is the evidence it added a capability rather than changed a behaviour. Two things the tests pin that reading the diff will not tell you: the injected component must receive `href` as a real **prop** (Inertia's `Link` declares it; as a fallthrough attribute the anchor looks right and never becomes a client visit), and a call site must pass a **`markRaw`** component or Vue warns about deep-proxying a component through a reactive props bag.

  **⚠️ AND IN A TEMPLATE THE PROP IS `:ariaLabel`, NOT `:aria-label` — A GATE FAILURE WITH NO OBVIOUS CAUSE.** Vue's runtime camelizes hyphenated prop names, but `vue-tsc` keeps `aria-label` as an HTML attribute because it is a real one: the kebab spelling type-checks as an *attribute* and the required `ariaLabel` **prop** then reads as missing. Recorded in DSR §3.4 and in both call sites, because "tidying" it back to kebab is the obvious thing for the next author to do.

  **THREE USER DECISIONS 2026-08-11 (the Vue half), DO NOT RE-ASK.** (1) the `linkComponent` prop above; (2) **the builder gets the BREADCRUMB ONLY, not the strip** — it is a three-pane workspace on a `height:100%` grid and a second ~44px header row costs the one screen that cannot spare it, so `Forms / {title} / Builder` is its way back and DSR §3.4 carries the split; (3) **`forms/Index.vue`'s row title was PULLED FORWARD from J2d** — it linked to the builder and only `v-if="row.can.edit"`, so a non-editor got inert text, and without it the hub would have shipped with no inbound link from the forms list at all.

  **⚠️ SHARE IS NOT A TAB, AND THE APPROVED PLAN'S TABLE SAID IT WAS — a recorded deviation, not a silent one.** That table listed Share as a fifth strip item "opening `ShareModal` on the hub", which is exactly the `TabNav`-versus-`Tabs` confusion DSR §3.4 exists to prevent: every item in the strip is a URL with its own route and its own gate, and a modal-opener is neither. It would put an `aria-current`-capable link in the strip whose activation navigates nowhere. Share ships as a **`PageHeader` action button** gated on the presence of the `share` key; the builder keeps its own toolbar button, so J2b widened Share's reach rather than moving it. DSR §3.4 carries the correction.

  **⚠️ THREE CRUMBS, NEVER TWO, ON A FORM'S SUB-PAGE.** `MdsBreadcrumb` renders the LAST item as text whatever it carries, so the natural-looking `Forms / {title}` prints the hub's name **with no link on it** — the dead end intact, now with a separator. Both the builder and the analytics page end on their own name. Consequence worth knowing before writing a locator: a form page now carries **two** `aria-current="page"` elements (the trail's tail and the strip's active tab). That is correct, ARIA sets no uniqueness constraint, axe raises nothing — but a page-wide `[aria-current="page"]` matches the BREADCRUMB first, which is how the first draft of `show.test.ts` asserted the wrong element.

  | webhooks | `WebhookEndpointPresenter::index(User)` :43 | **NO** | — | — |

Client: **Style B with an UNCONDITIONAL `<h2>`** (`PageHeader` renders the `<h1>` and `MdsEmptyState` an `<h3>`, so dropping it fails axe heading-order ONLY in the empty state - the state a filter creates most), `replace: true`, and the keyword input **NOT** `:disabled="busy"` (it blurs and eats the caret mid-word); one-shot selects keep `:disabled`.

  **J1d - the ⌘K command palette (BUILT).** `GET /search/suggest` returns **plain JSON, never an Inertia partial** - a partial re-dispatches the CURRENT page's controller on every request, so each debounce tick on `/forms/{form}/builder` would re-run a full builder render to fetch five rows. Synchronous, no job, no storage — unlike the submission PDF, which is queued precisely because it STORES an artifact against the tenant's quota. **UNGATED by plan on purpose:** the obvious-looking `feature:ocr_single` is Professional+, and printing a blank form is useful with no OCR anywhere in the picture. **A DRAFT 404s** — not a policy preference: a draft's `schema_snapshot` is literally `[]`, so without the guard the request 200s with a titled document containing NO QUESTIONS, failing as "an empty form" rather than "a refused one". **A SUPERSEDED version still prints**, which is the case the OCR chain needs: paper already in the field was printed against the layout live at the time.

A presenter that renders the list as it arrives produces a shuffled form that is entirely plausible on any single example. The ordering test's fixture has its `key` order as the exact REVERSE of its `sequence` order, so a presence-only assertion cannot pass by accident.

(2) **`.runhead`'s offsets are page-CONTENT-relative**: `Positioner\Absolute::position()` places a fixed BLOCK at `containing_block + top` and `determine_absolute_containing_block()` gives a fixed frame the page box AFTER the `@page` margins — so `top` is negative on purpose, and that branch **never reads `right`**, which is why the width is explicit. Found by reading `vendor/dompdf`, not by looking at a PDF. Also: **no page numbers and no barcode are possible** — page counters go through `page_text()` (inline PHP, disabled by the §5 security contract) and any raster needs `ext-gd`, absent from the app container and all four CI jobs.

Paper can narrow nothing, so it is now a **comb with one captioned run per declared level**, which is what a paper address block has always looked like. The cause was a real bug: the service **stored `$normalized` (un-pruned) while projecting `$final` (pruned)**, so after every edit the JSONB answer document and the typed index disagreed, and an answer the original submit had pruned as irrelevant was resurrected. Both finalize doors store the pruned document; this one did not. Fixed, and the clock mutation now reddens with exactly the right message ("Failed asserting that an array has the key 'same_day_note'") — **a wrong clock silently DELETES an answer that was relevant when the response was filed.**

  **⚠️ THE LOST-UPDATE GUARD HAD TO MOVE TO THE CLIENT, AND THE FIRST VERSION WAS SECURITY THEATRE.** The write is a whole-document replace, so a second editor saving a stale page reverts everything the first corrected — silently, with an audit row diffed against the stale snapshot that says nothing about the reversion. The first attempt compared a value read at the top of `edit()` against one read under the lock, **which is always equal**, because both reads happen inside one request with nothing interleaved. The lost update spans two REQUESTS. What shipped is an optimistic-concurrency **baseline** (`answers_content_checksum`) emitted by the presenter, carried on the PATCH, and compared server-side — the same posture `routes/tenant.php` already records for the builder ("content edits carry an `updated_at` token → 409 on drift"). It also closes browser-Back-then-Save. **The rule is `present` + `nullable`, NOT `required`**: the column is nullable, so a submission stored before the pipeline stamped a checksum would otherwise be permanently uneditable.

The success toast names the outcome, because `demotes_on_save` is a page-load snapshot and a reviewer can approve in another tab.

Gate `native_connectors` Starter+, INHERITED — no new gate, no new ability, no new `UsageMetric`, no new `QueueName`. **FOUR DECISIONS LOCKED WITH THE USER UP FRONT:** (1) a row carries **MAPPED ANSWERS**, not the metadata envelope; (2) scopes are **per-file, never all-Drive**; (3) **pre-flight refresh + corrected classification**; (4) drift **pauses the rule and notifies the owner**. **THE SHARED ENGINE IS `App\Support\Mapping\*`** — `ColumnFingerprint` / `ColumnMapping` / `MappedColumn` / `MappingDrift` / `MappingDriftDetector`, pure (no HTTP, no Eloquent, no container) and pinned by `MappingNamespaceBoundaryTest`, which PARSES the namespace's own source and fails if it imports from Connectors/Ocr/Database/Http. **BOTH DIRECTIONS SHIP NOW** — `project()` writes (H16a) and `interpret()` reads (H19a's linelist) — so the reuse is demonstrable rather than asserted; a one-directional engine is exactly how H19a would have discovered the shape did not fit and written a second one. **ORDER IS PART OF THE FINGERPRINT** because both consumers address columns positionally; a set-based digest would call a reordered sheet identical and put every answer under the wrong heading, which is the failure `ocr-pipeline-design.md:84` names. **VERIFICATION NARROWED A LOCKED DECISION, IN THE DIRECTION THE USER CHOSE:** the plan said add `spreadsheets` only if required — Google's own scope table classifies `drive.file` **Recommended, Non-sensitive** for the Sheets API and `spreadsheets` **Sensitive**, so `drive.file` ships ALONE, avoiding both the wider grant and Google's sensitive-scope verification tier. **THE SHARPEST FACT IN THE INCREMENT: Google answers HTTP 401 `authError` for an EXPIRED access token and a REVOKED grant alike.** Only the token endpoint distinguishes them (`invalid_grant`), so the adapter classifies 401 as **retryable**; the obvious mapping would have revoked a live connection roughly once an hour, clearing both tokens and emailing the owner each time. **FOUR NET-NEW FRAMEWORK CHANGES, each because the alternative was wrong:** a **fourth `ConnectorDeliveryResult` outcome `blocked`** (destination unusable, credential healthy → pause ONE rule; `failed` would retry a human-only fix and `credentialRejected` would revoke a good grant over one added column); **`ConnectionTokenRefresher::ensureFresh()`** (ADR-0009 §D6's own revisit trigger, fired — Google's ~1h tokens vs an hourly sweep — as a 120s GUARD on top of the sweep, not a second policy); a **`$terminal` flag on `ConnectorOAuthException`** (the refresher marked a grant permanently dead on ANY exception **including a transport timeout** — unreachable in H15a because Slack tokens never expire, reachable on every Google send from here, and found because PHPStan reported the adapter's CREDENTIAL_ERRORS constant as unused); and **`SubscriptionConfigRules`**, because H15a's four request classes hard-coded Slack's `config.channel_id` in the shared layer, so a Sheets rule was rejected by validation before any adapter saw it. **Two more Slack-shaped seams in provider-agnostic code fixed:** `ConnectorChannelDirectory::message()` said "Slack" in every string, and `ConnectionPresenter::providerDescription()` is a `default`-less `match` that would have thrown `UnhandledMatchError` on the Integrations page. **`valueInputOption=RAW` IS A SECURITY CONTROL, not formatting:** `security-threat-model.md:127`'s formula-injection row in a worse form — a live Sheet evaluates `=IMPORTXML(...)` on GOOGLE'S servers with no human opening anything — and RAW is structural where the CSV path still owes a `'` prefix (that row stays OPEN). `insertDataOption=INSERT_ROWS` because the API DEFAULTS to OVERWRITE, which would destroy whatever the tenant keeps below their table. **`SubmissionRowProjector` EXTRACTED from `SubmissionExporter`** so a synced row and a downloaded row cannot disagree — the seam is a `fieldKey ⇒ value` MAP, not a positional row, because the two consumers order columns differently and neither ordering is more correct. **13 MUTATIONS RUN; ONE CAME BACK GREEN AND INDICTED THE CODE:** the `! $alreadyPaused` edge-trigger was unreachable (the job's own Active-status guard already stops every queued delivery behind the first block), so the flag and its comment are GONE and the test now drives TWO deliveries to pin the real mechanism. **TWO PROCESS LESSONS, both about mutations that lie.** A `sed` whose pattern never matched (`\x1E` in a BRE reduces to `x1E`) and a mutation that introduced a SYNTAX ERROR both reported "green"/"red" for reasons unrelated to the code — **verify a mutation actually applied, and `php -l` it, before believing either colour**. A third mutation was behaviourally EQUIVALENT (`$valuesByFieldKey[null]` coerces to `['']`), which looked like a test gap and was not. **Also: `git checkout --` after a mutation reverts to the COMMITTED state, silently undoing uncommitted work in the same file.** **TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY RE-READING THE ADAPTER AFTER THE SUITE WAS ALREADY GREEN, not by a failing test:** (1) **a sheet name went into A1 notation UNQUOTED** — and Google's own default tab for a form-linked sheet is `Form Responses 1`, with spaces, so `Form Responses 1!1:1` is unparseable and an entirely ordinary destination would have failed; worse, it fails as a **400**, which the classifier treated as transient, so it would have burned the whole seven-day ladder and dead-lettered with the tenant never told why. Quoting is now unconditional, with an internal apostrophe DOUBLED per A1's own rule. (2) **a 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENT` is also Google's answer for a TAB THAT NO LONGER EXISTS** — the likeliest way a working rule breaks after setup — so it is now `blocked` rather than retried. Both are pinned (reverting the quoting reddens 2, reverting the 400 arm reddens 1). **AND THE `git checkout --` TRAP BIT A THIRD TIME IN ONE SESSION**, discarding both of these while they were still uncommitted and making one mutation run measure unfixed code — **commit BEFORE mutating, every time**. **KNOWN NARROWINGS, recorded not discovered later:** no identity scope ⇒ `external_account_id` is a constant ⇒ **one live Google connection per tenant** (a second replaces the first); **no `channel_lister`** (per-file access cannot enumerate — the picker is H16b's client-side Google Picker); **event-driven append only** (scheduled sync + historical backfill are named out of scope); and the exported `openapi.json` shows every destination key as optional, because which are required depends on the connection's provider — **and that contract nearly regressed silently**: Scramble reads `rules()` statically, so returning the whole shape from a method degraded `config` to an array-of-strings, which the CI gate could NOT catch because it only diffs a fresh export against the committed file and both were equally wrong. Fixed with a static `documentedShape()` union plus dynamic `requiredFor()`. **Docs: ADR-0009 §D6 + §D8 amended in place with the reasoning (both revisit triggers fired) and its "When to Revisit" first bullet answered; `data-privacy-gdpr-compliance.md` §7 revised IN THIS INCREMENT as that bullet itself demanded — the connector envelope is no longer metadata-by-default, and the erasure asymmetry (a row already in the tenant's Drive cannot be recalled) is recorded; `webhook-integration-design.md` §4 row 4 built-note; threat-model addendum; data-dictionary §25 `config` shape.**

- **H25 (as-built, MERGED PR #93 `c2e0223`, 6/6 CI green on the FIRST run — Contract 48s, frontend 1m15s, static 1m41s, a11y 2m11s, Pest 3m53s, E2E 11m17s) — the R5 published-version immutability guard, and the schema's FIRST database trigger.** Ships **ADR-0013 in-PR** (the H22a/ADR-0012 precedent). **R5 had been open since the architecture doc was written** and was one of only two rows in the §9 register still marked *Still OPEN*; it lost its forcing moment when the 2026-07-21 decision chose relevance-derived step-skipping over a stored step graph, and became this hardening PR. **THE GAP, PRECISELY:** a published version's CONTENT has been frozen in Postgres since Increment D (`draftChildGuard` gates every child write behind `EXISTS (fv.status = 'draft')`), but its OWN ROW was not — `formVersionGuard` leaves UPDATE deliberately status-blind so publish can flip draft→published→superseded, so `schema_snapshot`, `checksum`, `version_number`, `title`, `published_at` were all freely rewritable on a live published row, **and `status` could be set back to `'draft'`, which RE-OPENS every child row, because the child guard keys on exactly that value**. **RLS structurally cannot close it and this is not a preference:** a policy sees only OLD in `USING` and only NEW in `WITH CHECK`, and no clause can compare them, while a per-column immutability rule IS that comparison; a CHECK cannot see OLD either. **AS BUILT:** `form_versions_published_immutable_trg`, `BEFORE UPDATE … FOR EACH ROW`, gated `WHEN (OLD.status IS DISTINCT FROM 'draft')` — the gate keys on `OLD.status` and NEVER on `published_at`, because `ConnectorFanOutTest:146` legitimately writes `published_at` onto a draft row, and it lives in the `WHEN` clause and nowhere else (two copies drift, and the drift direction where WHEN fires but the body early-returns is fail-open — plus `pg_get_triggerdef()` then carries the predicate, which is what the structural test pins). **(1) DENY BY DEFAULT is the whole design** — there is NO list of frozen columns, because a hand-list is fail-OPEN for the future (a column added later would be silently mutable and nothing in CI would notice: `scripts/migration-lint.php` early-returns on alter-only migrations, so this migration's own green is VACUOUS and the three test files are the only things standing over the guard). It diffs the WHOLE ROW, `to_jsonb(OLD)` vs `to_jsonb(NEW)` per key, against a four-name allowlist — a feature test adds a column inside the test transaction and proves it is already frozen. **(2) Compared as `::text`, not as jsonb** — jsonb equality is numeric-aware (`'1'::jsonb = '1.0'::jsonb` is TRUE), so a scale-only rewrite would pass a jsonb `=` guard while silently invalidating `checksum`, which is SHA-256 over the canonical TEXT and is the offline-sync cache-buster; `::text` still treats a key-reordered snapshot as unchanged (jsonb normalises key order at parse time), and both halves are tested. The projection is also NULL-safe by construction (a SQL NULL becomes the jsonb value `null`), which matters because SEVEN frozen columns are nullable — including `created_at`, since `timestampsTz()` emits both timestamps nullable — and the suite routinely makes published rows with a NULL `checksum`; **no bare `<>` appears anywhere and a unit test asserts that absence**. **(3) FOUR INDEPENDENT RULES, not chained** (a bare `updated_at` touch on a superseded row must pass, or the guard is stricter than the invariant): frozen columns; `status` may only move `published → superseded`, `superseded` terminal, **never back to draft**; `superseded_at` writable only by that flip and only out of NULL; and **`published_by` may be CLEARED but never re-pointed**. **THAT FOURTH RULE IS THE ONE THAT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED THIS BROKEN and it is not obvious:** `published_by` is `ON DELETE SET NULL` against `users`, and PostgreSQL runs that referential action as an ordinary UPDATE through SPI — **it bypasses RLS but NOT a trigger** — so freezing the column outright would have made user hard-deletion (and GDPR erasure with it) permanently impossible, raising a form-version error from an unrelated tenant's row on a statement about `users`. A feature test hard-deletes a publisher and asserts the version survives with a null attribution (the publisher must be a distinct user from the form owner — `forms.owner_user_id` is `ON DELETE NO ACTION` — and an active member, because `users` carries a join-shape SELECT policy and Postgres applies SELECT policies to a WHERE-qualified DELETE, so a non-member would match zero rows and the test would pass vacuously). **(4) Refusals raise SQLSTATE 23001** (`restrict_violation`) naming every offending column (`string_agg`, alphabetical), the row id and the status — unambiguous here because Postgres core never emits it (a RESTRICT FK raises 23503) and nothing else in the codebase does, which is also what proves the TRIGGER refused a write and not the policy (an RLS `WITH CHECK` failure is 42501, and BEFORE ROW triggers run first). **Deliberately NO renderer in `bootstrap/app.php`:** reaching this guard means a code path bypassing the service layer, and a loud 500 is correct — mapping it to a friendly error would normalise exactly what R5 exists to surface. **SCOPE IS UPDATE ONLY, AND THE RESIDUAL IS NEW RISK R12** (user decision, taken before building): a `BEFORE DELETE` row trigger fires on FK cascades too, so it would turn tenant hard-delete and form hard-delete into an error, and would break `SavedReportViewWebTest:239`. So a `forms`/`tenants` hard-delete still wipes published versions through the cascade (referential actions bypass RLS) and `TRUNCATE` bypasses row triggers entirely — recorded as **R12** with a revisit trigger (the first production hard-delete path) rather than silently inherited. **The guarantee is worded "a published version cannot be EDITED", never "cannot be destroyed", everywhere it appears.** **A COMPANION `form_versions_status_chk` SHIPS IN THE SAME MIGRATION and is not scope creep** — `status` was a bare `varchar(20)` with no CHECK, and the trigger TURNS THAT INTO A TRAP by treating anything that is not `'draft'` as frozen, so one typo'd status would freeze a row permanently in a state no code can read. **`CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` IS MANDATORY, NOT STYLISTIC, AND CI CANNOT CATCH IT:** `db:wipe` drops tables/views/types and NEVER routines, so `DROP TABLE … CASCADE` takes the trigger while the function survives — a bare `CREATE FUNCTION` dies on the SECOND `migrate:fresh` on any database, which every CI job avoids by provisioning a fresh one, so it would ship green and break only developers. Verified by running `migrate:fresh` twice. `down()` drops trigger-then-function (the trigger DEPENDS on the function) and never `CASCADE`s. **NAMING — this PR names the convention**, since the repo had zero triggers, trigger functions, `DB::unprepared` or `plpgsql` anywhere: **`_trg` for a trigger, `_fn` for its function, same base name, the table prefixing the function** (function names are schema-global, trigger names are per-table), all under the 63-byte `NAMEDATALEN` that truncates SILENTLY. **THREAT MODEL, STATED HONESTLY RATHER THAN OVERCLAIMED:** `meridian_app` OWNS the table, so it can `ALTER TABLE … DISABLE TRIGGER`; a superuser can `SET session_replication_role = 'replica'`. That is the asymmetry with RLS, where `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` was chosen *precisely because* it binds the owner — so this is an **integrity guard against application bugs and raw queries** (R5's own wording is "accidentally mutates"), **not a security boundary**. What it DOES add over RLS: it binds `pgsql_privileged` (a real superuser bypasses RLS and never a trigger — its own test pack, which needs a COMMITTED fixture on that connection or it passes vacuously, since RefreshDatabase wraps only the default one), and it fires on referential actions. **No GUC hatch** (a custom `app.*` GUC is settable by any role, so it would be no obstacle to the threat); the break-glass is written down instead — `DISABLE TRIGGER` … `ENABLE TRIGGER` inside its own migration, loud and reviewable. Trigger left in origin mode (`tgenabled = 'O'`), not `ENABLE ALWAYS`, which would fire during logical-replication apply and break a future replica restore replaying a supersede. **ONE LIVE DEFECT CLOSED IN PASSING, and it was the one reachable production path into this hole:** `FormService::updateMetadata()` wrote `title`/`description` to `whereKey($form->draft_version_id)` from an IN-MEMORY `$form`, with no lock and no re-read — so if that model was loaded before a concurrent publish, an ordinary form-settings save silently rewrote a PUBLISHED version's title, which is literally the R5 bug; now predicated on `status = 'draft'` so the stale write degrades to a no-op. **ONE DRIFTED FACT CORRECTED:** `FormBuilderService::rowVersion()`'s docblock claimed microsecond precision — Laravel's `Schema\Builder::$defaultTimePrecision` is 0 and the repo never overrides it, so the column is `timestamp(0)`; the real consequence (two builder edits inside one second are an undetectable lost update) is RECORDED, not fixed here, because it is not R5. **DELIBERATELY NOT CLOSED, recorded rather than built:** `draft → superseded` directly (the trigger is silent on draft rows by construction, and firing on them is what the operation-scoping forbids); it is a lifecycle bug, not an immutability breach, because nothing was ever published. **Docs: ADR-0013 + reconciliations to seven siblings** — `form-versioning-schema-migration.md` (**v1.1**, new §2.1: §2's "RLS, not a trigger" resolution STANDS for the three child tables and is narrowed to them, with the boundary stated once — *row-scoped ⇒ RLS, OLD-vs-NEW ⇒ trigger, one member today*), `architecture/technical-architecture.md` (R5 → **RESOLVED**, **new R12**, §6.2 point 4's note amended where it asserted "one single DB-level-guard idiom", Appendix A item 5 closed — and promoted to an ADR exactly as that appendix's closing line anticipated), `data-dictionary.md` §3 (the file had NO mention of any immutability guard), `adr/0002` (a *narrowed, not superseded* note — it is what made "RLS is the one idiom" load-bearing), `workflow-branching-design.md` (§1 and the deferred list both pointed at H25), `testing-strategy.md` (the pack, plus the three reusable harness rules it encodes), `PRD.md` (ADR index). **Gates: Pest 2201 (+52 — 17 unit + 32 feature + 3 privileged), full suite green**; PHPStan **exactly 55**, the documented local phantom baseline, **zero introduced, verified PER FILE** (the two naming `FormBuilderService` are the pre-existing `FormField::$created_by`/`$updated_by` phantoms whose line numbers merely moved 9 down); Pint / controller-gate / migration-lint / job-payload-lint green; **no `openapi.json` change** (DDL-only cannot drift Scramble), no frontend change, golden corpora byte-untouched. The 1400s suite time is the documented host-memory-pressure artifact, not this branch.

(The local dev DB is EMPTY — 0 tenants, 0 forms — so the manual browser check in the plan was deliberately NOT done rather than seed the user's environment uninvited; CI's E2E covers the same ground.) Built off `main`, NOT off #97, exactly as row 258 scopes it (tokens + offline cache-invalidation; the logo is not in it). **THE APPLICATION HALF IS THE EASY HALF AND IT STILL HAD ONE TRAP.** The guest shell can never carry `data-theme-mode`, so a guest-specific two-block emission naming only `:root` looked obviously right and is WRONG: inside `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` a bare `:root` is (0,1,0) and **loses** to `theme-overrides.css`'s own system-dark block at `:root:not([data-theme-mode='light']):not([data-theme-mode='dark'])` — (0,3,0). Still read through `isActive()` and never `hasBrandRamp()` — a downgraded tenant keeps its stored ramp and renders unbranded, pinned by its own test. **ONE LIVE DEFECT CLOSED IN PASSING, on exactly this surface, and the user approved it before building:** the shell's `<meta name="theme-color">` and `PwaManifestController::THEME_COLOR` were both hard-coded `#1B5E5E` = `--mds-accent-teal-600` since G8a — but the guest shell has NEVER emitted `data-accent`, so it paints Blueprint, and the browser chrome plus the installed app's splash screen were tinted a colour appearing **nowhere in the form**. `theme-color` now means one thing in both cases — the light `--mds-color-action-primary-bg` — tenant-derived when branded, `--mds-primary-600` (`#1C4B72`) when not. `background_color` stays `--mds-neutral-50`: §D7 keeps the tenant layer off neutrals, and the two sit adjacent in one payload, which is where that rule is easiest to break. **THE OFFLINE HALF IS THE HARD HALF, AND THE DESIGN DECISION IS "RE-PRIME, NEVER PURGE."** The brand rides the shell HTML, which the SW caches `NetworkFirst` under `guest-shell-html` — so the page in front of the respondent self-heals on any successful online load and needs no invalidation. What does not self-heal is every OTHER `/f/…` shell the device cached earlier (a second form, a resume link), stale until its 7-day expiry. **`caches.delete('guest-shell-html')` is the obvious fix and it is the wrong one**: a stale brand is COSMETIC, a purged shell costs a fieldworker offline access to a form they deliberately primed, which is a core PRD promise — a bad trade in any brand's favour. That negative is the single most important behaviour in the file and has its own test. The manifest link carries the same fingerprint as `?b=` because the SW never caches that URL and the browser caches it hard; safe for app identity, since the manifest declares an explicit `id` so the URL is not what pins an installed app. `guest-schema` / `guest-shell-assets` untouched — neither carries brand. Dexie goes to **v2** for the new `app_state` store (a new STORE needs a bump; G8c's un-indexed `conflict_code` correctly did not), with a test proving the v1 outbox survives the upgrade — a bump that dropped a respondent's queued work for a cosmetic feature would be the worst possible trade here. **ONE TEST-HARNESS TRAP WORTH CARRYING, AND IT MAKES A CORRECT PRODUCT LOOK BROKEN:** the natural proof that "the fingerprint moves when the brand moves" is to re-brand mid-test and re-render — and it FAILS, because within one Pest test the container keeps the `Tenant` bound by the FIRST request (stancl `Tenancy::initialize()` early-returns when the tenant key is unchanged, `Tenancy.php:43`), so the second render reports the OLD ramp. That one axis moved to the `<html>` **open tag** (what the invariant was always about); the other three stayed whole-document, and a new case proves the root element is attribute-free **while the brand block is present**, asserted as a user with maximal preferences. **Gates: Pest 2287 (+11), full suite green; Vitest 1189 (+8, 55 files); vue-tsc BOTH tsconfigs, Vite build, Pint, controller-gate / migration-lint / job-payload-lint all clean; PHPStan exactly 55, zero introduced, VERIFIED PER FILE (none of the three touched/new PHP files appears in the breakdown). No migration, no `/api/v1` route, `openapi.json` byte-identical.** Docs: ADR-0014 as-built (the fifth consuming surface, and it CAN resolve `var()` — so §D8's revisit trigger, which asks for a SIXTH, does not fire), `offline-first-sync-design.md` **§4.1 new** (the re-prime rule + the `app_state` store), DSR §2.9 governing rule, `testing-strategy.md` (three generalising lessons). **ADR-0014's two stale Consequences paragraphs were deliberately NOT touched — PR #97 already strikes both through in place, and duplicating that here guarantees a conflict when #97 lands.**
