- **H5c (as-built)** — the **entitlement RETRO-GATE** (ADR-0008 §D4/§D5/§D7, pricing-matrix §2/§3; depends H5b), closing the three things H5b deferred. **(1) The grandfather storage + merge-day backfill.** New strict-RLS **`legacy_overrides`** table — one row per tenant, a `feature_flags` JSONB override map, **`bigint identity` PK** (internal per-tenant state, the `usage_counters` precedent → no `HasUuidv7`; also makes the raw-SQL backfill trivial, no uuid-in-SQL on PG17). `EntitlementService::legacyOverrides()` now reads it (memoized per tenant — `snapshot()` calls `feature()` once per flag key), consulted AHEAD of the plan flags (the existing `array_key_exists` precedence); `forget()` clears it too. The **merge-day backfill** is the G10a `CollaboratorBackfill` pattern exactly: a *separate*, later-timestamped migration (`2026_07_23_000005`, `$withinTransaction=false`) delegating to a reusable, pure-unit-tested `LegacyOverrideBackfill` body that runs ONE cross-tenant `INSERT … SELECT FROM tenants … ON CONFLICT (tenant_id) DO NOTHING` on **`pgsql_privileged`** (BYPASSRLS — the app connection under FORCE RLS with no tenant GUC would stamp zero tenants), grandfathering the five keys. On `migrate:fresh` (empty DB) it stamps nothing (born-gated); it only bites against a live, populated DB on deploy. **(2) Feature-gating the five capabilities** via a new **`feature:<key>` middleware** (`RequireFeature`, first consumer of `feature()`) throwing **`FeatureGateException`** (402, `feature_not_available`, `{feature}` details; rendered API-envelope / web-toast like `QuotaExceededException`). **The linchpin decision: the gate blocks ONLY when a plan RESOLVES and denies the feature** — a null (unseeded/dev) plan passes through, the same "no catalog ⇒ no enforcement" stance as `QuotaGuard`'s null-quota, so the ~1150-test plan-free suite stays inert and only the new H5c tests seed plans. Gated (web + `/api/v1`): `xlsform_export`, `form_templates`, `field_library`; **`api_access` = one choke point** on the whole Group-B stack (after `AuthenticateApiToken`) + `POST auth/tokens` mint (list/revoke stay ungated); **`offline_sync`** gates the offline ENTRY only — the guest PWA manifest (in-controller 404, not the redirect-y middleware, since it's not `/api/v1`) + the authenticated `sync/manifest` — **not** `/sw.js` (no tenant context) and **not** `sync/submissions` (never-block replay, §D4), and the main guest form page `/f/{slug}` is untouched (respondents always reach it). **`form_templates`/`field_library` were NOT seeded flag keys** (route names only in Phase 2) → added to `PlanCatalog` at **Starter+** (matrix §3 + this increment). **(3) The `api_requests` monthly-quota 429**: new **`QuotaGuard::assertWithinRateQuota()`** (RateLimit class) + **`RateLimitExceededException`** (429 + `Retry-After` to the period reset) + **`EnforceApiRequestQuota`** middleware after the api_access gate + throttle, before `MeterApiUsage` (so a 429'd request is not itself metered). **A null OR 0 quota never 429s** — 0 is the Free "no access" sentinel, reached only via a grandfather override, so a grandfathered Free tenant's granted `api_access` is not hollowed by its 0 quota. **`webhook_deliveries` = reusable seam** (the guard method + exception work for it; no dispatch code until H13 — no middleware/route). **Client-hide** (rule #3): `entitlements` prop typed in `inertia.d.ts` + a `useEntitlements()` composable; gated affordances hidden in `Builder.vue` (XLSForm buttons, Fields⇄Library toggle) + `forms/Index.vue` (template links, save-as-template). **Gates: Pest 1186 (+35)** across 7 files (`LegacyOverrideBackfill` unit; Feature `LegacyOverride`/`RateQuotaGuard`/`OfflineSyncGate`/`FeatureGateWeb`/`ApiAccessGate`/`ApiRequestQuota`); PHPStan L8 ZERO on every new file (one `nullsafe.neverNull` fixed the H5a `tier()` way — explicit `=== null`); Pint / migration-lint / job-payload-lint / controller-gate green; vue-tsc clean; **no `openapi.json` drift** (middleware-only route changes). Migrations: `legacy_overrides` DDL (`…000004`) + backfill (`…000005`). Narrowing: the backfill's populated cross-boundary run is proven by the migration + the behavioural `LegacyOverrideTest` (not a RefreshDatabase test — the privileged session can't see uncommitted test tenants, the G10a limitation); the super-admin console plan-selector UI stays deferred.
- **H5b (as-built)** — **entitlement ENFORCEMENT** (ADR-0008 §D4/§D8/§D9, pricing-matrix §2/§4; depends H5a). Makes the H5a read-model *bite*, along the three ratified classes. **The enforcement CLASSIFIER is now code, not prose**: new `EnforcementMode` enum (HardBlock/NeverBlock/RateLimit/Unclassified) + `UsageMetric::enforcementMode()`/`isGauge()` (the `ResourceCapacity::anyPermission()` precedent — promoted from the H5a docblock; `values()` untouched so the DB CHECK is unaffected). **Gauges are enforced by a LIVE COUNT/SUM under RLS, never a running aggregate** (the H12a `max_responses` precedent + the G10a/H2 "a synced counter is a landmine" lesson — gauges move *down* on archive/delete/remove): new `EntitlementService::countGauge()` (non-memoized, the guard's authoritative pre-write read) + `liveGauge()` (memoized, for the read-model); `usage()` now branches gauge→live / flow→counter so `snapshot()` shows a just-created form immediately. **`QuotaGuard::assertCanCreate(metric, incoming=1)`** (scoped) throws **`QuotaExceededException`** (402, metric-specific `code()`, `{metric,limit,used}` details; rendered in `bootstrap/app.php` — API envelope, web toast) when `quota !== null && countGauge + incoming > limit`; null quota (unlimited / off-tenant / unseeded catalog) never blocks — **which is why the pre-H5b suite, seeding no plans, is inert**. Three hard-block sites: `FormService::create` (top of its tx — covers template-instantiate transitively, the sole `Form::create`), `AttachmentStorageService::store` (**staff only — `$uploadedBy!==null`; a GUEST respondent's upload is NEVER blocked**, the same never-block principle as submissions, since it is the same choke point for both), `TenantMembershipService::invite` (**reserve-on-invite** — counts Active+Invited, blocks a genuinely-new seat; accept is count-neutral; decline/remove free it). **Never-block `submissions_count`**: a **synchronous, auto-discovered** `MeterSubmissionUsage` listener on the post-commit/created-only `SubmissionCreated` increments via **`UsageMeter`** (concurrency-safe `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (tenant_id,metric,period_start) DO UPDATE`, whole body swallow-and-logged so a broken meter can never lose a respondent's already-committed data). `exports_count` metered at `SubmissionExporter::stream`; `api_requests` metered by a new **`MeterApiUsage`** middleware on the Group-B stack (after auth+throttle — **meter only; the monthly-quota 429 is H5c**, to avoid back-dooring an API feature-gate before the grandfather override exists). **The cross-tenant rollup**: `RollUpUsageCountersJob` (a `MaintenanceJob`, ADR-0007 §D3) fans out one **`ReconcileTenantUsageJob`** (`TenantAwareJob`, `scheduled-maintenance`) per active tenant, which reconciles `submissions_count` from the authoritative `submissions` table (the never-block self-heal), materializes gauge levels + stamps `limit_snapshot`/`subscription_id`, and sends the never-block **`QuotaOverageNotification`** upsell once when submissions first cross quota; scheduled `dailyAt('02:40')`. **Rate-limit binding = forward seam** (decision): queue-fairness ceilings stay **uniform** (pricing-matrix §4); the §D9 `tier_resolver`/`tiers` config is left as the documented Phase-4 seam (untouched). `SuperAdminService::assignPlan` gains a `forget()` (first caller of the H5a seam). **Test-fixture churn**: `E2eSeeder` assigns `acme` a Professional plan (unlimited forms) so the ~10 seeded forms don't trip Free's cap; Pest gains `assignPlanTier()`/`assignUnlimitedPlan()`. **Gates: Pest +37** across 7 files (`EnforcementMode` unit; Feature `FormQuota`/`StorageQuota`/`SeatQuota`/`SubmissionNeverBlock`/`UsageMeter`/`UsageRollup` + extended `EntitlementService`/`ScheduleDeclaration`) — the rollup is a **committing** test (`config('queue.default')='database'` + `workOneJob('scheduled-maintenance')`, the `ProbeMaintenanceJob` precedent). PHPStan L8 ZERO on every new file; Pint / migration-lint / job-payload-lint (`QuotaOverageNotification` in `EXEMPT_JOBS`) green; **no migration** (`usage_counters` exists); no `openapi.json` drift (metering middleware is transparent, no route). **Discovered in build**: Laravel 11+ **auto-discovers** `app/Listeners` — a manual `Event::listen` double-registered the meter (double-counted submissions), so the listener is auto-discovered only. Narrowings: `api_requests`/`webhook_deliveries` monthly-quota enforcement + `api_access`/xlsform/etc. feature-gating are **H5c** (behind the grandfather override); gauge counter rows are reporting-only (`usage()` reads gauges live); an invite-of-an-already-invited-email resend is proven count-neutral by inspection (the `pgsql_auth` re-lookup can't commit under `RefreshDatabase`).
- **H5a (as-built)** — the **entitlement model** (the last of the four backend substrates; data-dictionary §16/§17/§18, ADR-0008; depends H1b/H2/H4). **100% net-new** — no entitlement code existed. Three string enums (`PlanTier` 5, `BillingInterval` 2, `UsageMetric` 7, each with `values()` feeding a DB CHECK); **deliberately NO `SubscriptionStatus`/`PlanStatus`** (`stripe_status` is free text; plans use `is_active`). Three tables: **`plans` is the ONE table with no `tenant_id`/no RLS** (global catalog; **NOT** added to `EXEMPT_TABLES` — migration-lint short-circuits on no-`tenant_id` tables; verified `relrowsecurity=f`); **`subscriptions`/`usage_counters` carry `tenant_id` + strict RLS** (`relrowsecurity=t/t`). `usage_counters.id` is **`bigint identity`** (so `UsageCounter` omits `HasUuidv7`). **`tenants` untouched** — by design no `plan_id`; current plan derives from the active subscription. Kept **Cashier-shaped, no Cashier** (Stripe columns dormant; admin-assigned). **`EntitlementService`** (`scoped()`, memoized per tenant — the `ResourceGrantResolver` precedent): `currentPlan()` = active subscription's plan (`Subscription::scopeActive` = `stripe_status∈{active,trialing}` ∧ `ended_at IS NULL`) else the seeded **`free`** fallback; `feature()`/`quota()`/`usage()` (0 in H5a — metering is H5b) + a `legacyOverrides()` **grandfather seam** (empty until H5c, resolves ahead of plan flags) + `snapshot()`. **Read-only "props" = a shared Inertia prop only** (`entitlements` in `HandleInertiaRequests::share()`, the `ui.theme` precedent) — **fail-closed off-tenant** (`snapshot()` null with no tenant context); **no styled page** (H5a is backend-only per rule #3). **Super-admin plan-assign** (`SuperAdminService::assignPlan` + `TenantAdminController::assignPlan` + `POST /admin/tenants/{tenant}/plan`): **adopt-tenant-context, NOT `elevated()`** (the H-map's literal wording superseded exactly as H4 dropped its own bypass) — one `DB::transaction`, adopt the affected tenant's context, upsert the `default` subscription **and** emit the **`subscription.updated`** audit (`AuditEvent::Updated` + `auditable_type='subscription'`, no enum change) atomically on the app connection, restore in `finally`; records the acting super-admin's `user_id` (`is_system_action=false`). **First new consumer of the H4 `AuditLogger`.** The **console selector UI is deferred** (a fast-follow; the admin `Tenants` page is a styled surface I can't verify locally — the backend assign is fully tested, mirroring H4 shipping the audits API with no UI screen). **`PlanSeeder`/`PlanCatalog`** seed all 5 tiers on the **default** connection (no RLS → no `pgsql_privileged` needed, least-privilege), idempotent on `code`, flags/quotas from pricing-matrix §2/§3 + ADR-0008 §D7 (`native_connectors`/`branding`=Starter+, `custom_domain`=Business), `business`/`enterprise` seeded `is_active=false` (held from sale, still admin-assignable); wired into `DatabaseSeeder`+`E2eSeeder`. **Gates: Pest 1113 (+22)** (`EntitlementEnums` unit; Feature `EntitlementService`/`PlanSeed`/`SubscriptionRls`/`SuperAdminAssignPlan`/`EntitlementsSharedProp`); **PHPStan L8 ZERO on every new H5a file** (full analyse back to the 77-error local baseline; two real new errors fixed in build — a `nullsafe.neverNull` on `tier()` restructured to an explicit `=== null`, and `findOrFail(mixed)` widening to `Plan|Collection` → `where('id',(string)…)->firstOrFail()`); Pint / migration-lint / controller-gate / job-payload-lint green; **no `openapi.json` drift** (no `/api/v1` route — assign is a web route, entitlements is a shared prop); `migrate:fresh --seed` green. Narrowings: usage metering + the rollup job are **H5b**; the grandfather override storage/backfill is **H5c**; the console plan-selector UI + a cross-tenant plan-listing console (an `elevated()` SELECT read) are deferred.
- **H1b (as-built)** — **ADR-0008 (entitlement & metering)**, a **docs-only** PR on the H1a/ADR-0007 precedent (Status/Context/Options/Drivers/Decision[blockquote+Concern|Choice+`Dn` bullets+Method note]/Consequences/Alternatives/When-to-Revisit/Related/References; **NO scorecard**). Ratifies the premises H5a builds on: **D1** admin-assigned plans, **no Cashier** (Stripe columns present but dormant — Phase-4 adoption is additive; `stripe_status` stays free text, no enum/CHECK); **D2** current plan = the active subscription's plan (no `tenants.plan_id`; "active" = `stripe_status∈{active,trialing}` ∧ `ended_at IS NULL`; unsubscribed ⇒ **free**); **D3** one `EntitlementService` reads `plans.feature_flags`+`plans.quotas` (null=unlimited), read-only in H5a; **D4** enforcement split — hard-block (`forms_count`/`storage_bytes`/`active_seats`), **never-block** (`submissions_count` — a respondent's data is never rejected for the tenant's billing), rate-limit (`api_requests`/`webhook_deliveries`); **D5** grandfather **indefinitely** via a per-tenant legacy override applied at H5c (seam ships in H5a); **D6** Business = build+gate, **hold from sale** until Track B (seeded `is_active=false`, admin-assignable), no 99.5% clause in Phase 3; **D7** `native_connectors`=Starter+, branding **unbundled**→Starter+, `custom_domain` stays Business; **D8** period-bounded `usage_counters` + `limit_snapshot`; **D9** usage rollup is a cross-tenant `MaintenanceJob` (ADR-0007 §D3); **D10** super-admin plan-assign audited via the **H4 `AuditLogger`** (`Updated`/`subscription`) under the affected tenant's adopted context — **not** `elevated()` (H-map wording superseded, mirroring H4's own dropped bypass), the first new consumer of the audit substrate. Doc reconciliation: `pricing-feature-gating-matrix.md` §3 gains the `native_connectors`+`branding` rows and an embedded-payments→Phase-4 annotation. Ships **docs-only** — no product code, no migration, no `ci.yml` change.
- **H4 (as-built)** — the **audit-log + ONE event-catalog substrate** (audit-compliance-logging-spec.md, data-dictionary §13/§22, tech-arch §4.1/§7.4), the next consumer of H2. **The `read:audit_log` ability and `audit_log.view` permission ALREADY existed** (seeded Owner+Admin, mapped in `ApiAbilities`) but were dead — no `audits` table/model/`Auditable` trait existed (0 migration hits) — so the catalog stays at **28 permissions** (no seeder/ability change); H4 fills the missing substrate. **Append-only ledger enforced at the DATABASE:** new `TenantIsolation::appendOnly` shape emits strict tenant SELECT + INSERT and **NO update/delete policy** — under FORCE RLS a policy-less command is denied for every role, so "immutable, never deleted" (§13) is a Postgres invariant, not a promise (mutation-proven: a raw UPDATE/DELETE returns 0 rows, the row is byte-unchanged). Deliberately **NOT `nullable_global`** (which widens SELECT to `OR tenant_id IS NULL` and would leak platform rows to every tenant — audits needs the opposite); `tenant_id` FK is **`nullOnDelete`, not cascade** (FK actions bypass RLS; a cascade would wipe the ledger on a tenant hard-delete). **The "one event catalog" is SEPARATE from audit, by design (§4.1 vs §7.4):** audit rows are written IN-transaction (atomic with the change) through one `AuditLogger` — there is **no `Auditable` model observer** in H4 (deferred to the first broad model-lifecycle increment); domain events are a POST-commit forward-seam for H13 webhooks + notifications. New abstract `DomainEvent` carries the envelope `{event_id (uuidv7, generated once), occurred_at, tenant_id, api_version, SCALAR data}` (§D5-safe, so H13 attaches a queued listener without touching an emission site); `DomainEventType` is the one catalog (`submission.created`, `form.published`). Per **user decision 1**, the pre-existing bare `SubmissionCreated` was **folded in** (scalar payload, no model) + the submission `created` audit written in the pipeline; new `FormPublished` raised post-commit by `PublishService`. **`AuditRedactor`** (pure, unit-tested) strips the fixed secret list + PII flags, records stripped names in `redacted_fields`, and handles the §2.1 erasure special case (both sides placeholdered) by construction. **6 `TODO(audits, Phase 1)` sites RETIRED** (grant→`created`, revoke→`deleted` with `old_values` captured *before* the hard-delete, `transferOwnership`→2×`permission_changed` against the `users` row + `tenant.updated`, publish→`published`, suspend/reactivate→`tenant.updated`) + the submission `created` audit. **Super-admin suspend/reactivate — a design refinement discovered in build:** rather than the planned elevated-connection + INSERT bypass, the audit is written UNDER the AFFECTED tenant's context on the app connection, **ATOMIC with the status change (one transaction)** — the strict INSERT passes with NO bypass or extra GRANT (least-privilege AND atomic, strictly better than the plan's best-effort split, and it sidesteps the cross-connection FK visibility problem the elevated path hit in tests). The planned `applySuperAdminBypass('audits',['INSERT'])` was **dropped as unused** (deferred to a future NULL-tenant platform-audit action). Records the acting super-admin's `user_id` (**user decision 2**; `is_system_action=false`, the tenant reads an opaque actor uuid its own `users` RLS can't resolve to a name); context save/restore via `applyLocal` so nothing leaks on the central host. **Read-only `GET /api/v1/audits`** (`ability:read:audit_log` + `can:viewAny,Audit`, cursor-paginated newest-first, RLS-scoped) + `AuditPolicy` (Owner/Admin) + `AuditResource` (returns already-redacted values); `openapi.json` regenerated (+`/audits`). **No UI screen** (spec §5 defers it; H4 is backend+api). **Gates: Pest 1091 (+27)** (`AuditRedactor`/`DomainEventEnvelope` unit + 3 `appendOnlySql` cases + Feature `AuditAppendOnlyRls`/`AuditSites`/`AuditSuperAdminSites`/`AuditApi`; full suite green under a 2G memory bump — the container's 128M CLI default OOMs the whole run, a known local artifact); **PHPStan L8 ZERO errors on every new H4 file** (app-wide baseline unchanged — the errors in edited files sit only in unchanged method bodies); Pint / migration-lint / controller-gate / job-payload-lint green; no `openapi.json` drift. Regression suites for the five modified services (Submissions/Scoping/Membership/Forms/Guest/Api/Admin, ~440 tests) all green — the added in-transaction audit writes broke nothing. **One CI-only follow-up:** the first `openapi.json` drifted because `scramble:export` had run before the `audits` table was migrated into the container's dev DB, so Scramble (which introspects DB column types) flattened every `AuditResource` field to `string`; regenerating **after** `php artisan migrate` produced the precise types CI expects (`is_system_action`→boolean, `user_id`/`ip_address`/`user_agent`→nullable, `redacted_fields`→`array|null`). **Gotcha to carry: always `migrate` before `scramble:export` or nullable/typed columns flatten to `string` and CI's drift diff fails.** Narrowings: no `Auditable` observer trait (deferred); super-admin SELECT bypass / cross-tenant audit search deferred to a support console; the redactor's `$piiAnswerKeys` branch is dormant until the `submissions.edit` fast-follow.

- **H3 (as-built)** — the **queued-mail substrate**, the first *consumer* of H2. Per user decision it takes ADR-0007's **framework-native** path (queued Notifications + the linter's now-populated `EXEMPT_JOBS`) over the recommended substrate-native `TenantAwareJob` wrapper, **and also queues the framework auth mail** (email verification + password reset). The engineering was making that path *safe* — three framework behaviours were **verified against `vendor/`** (the H2 lesson), and each shaped the design: **(1)** `NotificationSender::queueNotification` reads the **`#[Queue]` attribute** for notifications (`:246`), so the linter's R2 attribute and the *runtime* queue agree — no `viaQueues()` duplication; **(2)** `SendQueuedNotifications` serializes the notifiable via `SerializesModels` **before** the handler under a NULL GUC — so a queued `$user->notify()` would restore a `User` under fail-closed RLS (the §D5 hazard, worse for a *pending* invitee) → **every H3 mail is sent to an ON-DEMAND notifiable (`Notification::route('mail',$email)`) carrying SCALAR-only payload** (pre-built URLs + display strings resolved in-request), so no model is ever serialized and no tenant context is needed on the worker; **(3)** the fairness limiter closure returns `Limit::none()` for anything that is not a `TenantAwareJob` (`QueueServiceProvider:76`) — so **mail is deliberately NOT per-tenant fairness-limited** (documented; the new `mail` ceiling in `config/queue-fairness.php` is forward-looking for a future `TenantAwareJob` fan-out, commented as inert for queued notifications). New `QueueName::Mail = 'mail'` at **priority slot 3** (user-facing, above the pending-state queues, below `submissions`/`webhooks`), threaded **byte-identically** through the linter's `ALLOWED_QUEUE_CASES`, `config/queue-fairness.php`, the compose worker `--queue=`, `docs/deployment-infrastructure.md` §6/§8 and the observability doc — a test now guards `workerOrder()` === compose === docs (the one gate CI didn't enforce). `TenantInvitationNotification` → `ShouldQueue` + scalar (`tenantName` + a pre-built `acceptUrl` resolved in `TenantMembershipService::invite()` under live context — the old `acceptUrl()` moved to the service so no `Tenant` model rides the queue). Auth mail: `QueuedVerifyEmail`/`QueuedResetPassword` **subclass** the stock framework notifications and override only URL generation to return a pre-built scalar (reusing their wording/localization); `User::sendEmailVerificationNotification`/`sendPasswordResetNotification` sign the URL **in-request** (which also correctly captures the *request host*, unlike a naively-queued stock notification whose `toMail()` renders host-less on the worker). `app/Mail/TenantMail` is a thin **abstract, NOT-ShouldQueue** base — the H-map "app/Mail base" deliverable and forward seam for H9/H17 receipt/PDF Mailables (invisible to the job linter). **Gates: Pest +3 files** (`tests/Feature/Mail/QueuedMailContractTest` + `InvitationMailQueuedTest`, `tests/Feature/Auth/QueuedAuthMailTest`) + updated `MembershipLifecycleTest` (29 pass); Queue suite **44 unchanged**; **PHPStan level 8** clean on every H3 file (the 77 app-wide are the same documented local baseline, 0 on CI); `job-payload-lint` green (7 classes; `EXEMPT_JOBS` populated, R2/R3/R4 still enforced on exempt classes); Pint green. **Verification went two-process** (the path in-process tests structurally can't cover): a job dispatched to `mail` was drained by the real compose `worker` container and delivered to **Mailpit** with the correct subject and the pre-built signed URL in the body — proving the on-demand + scalar-URL override works end-to-end. Narrowings: mail is not fairness-limited (above); secret-in-queue accepted (invite/reset token + email transit `jobs`/`failed_jobs`, but token TTL 7d < failed-job retention 14d and `failed()` never logs the payload); `TenantMail` ships with no concrete subclass (forward seam by design).

- **H2 (as-built, split H2a + H2b per user decision)** — the async substrate proper, implementing ADR-0007 D1→D13. **The headline is that FIVE of the ADR's thirteen sub-decisions were contradicted by the installed framework (laravel/framework v13.18.1) and had to be corrected — the ADR itself (`:178`) instructed verifying its API claims at implementation time, and that instruction paid for itself five times.** Every correction is written back into ADR-0007 as a `> Corrected in H2 (as-built)` block, and every one is **proven by mutation**, not argued. **(1) §D4's after-edge is `JobAttempted`, not `JobProcessed`/`Queue::after`.** `Worker::process()` raises `JobProcessed` on the **success path only** (`:561`) and diverts to `handleJobException()` on a throw; `JobAttempted` is dispatched from the `finally` (`:566-570`). Implementing §D4 *literally* therefore leaks the tenant static out of **every job that throws or is released** — the §Context 6 defect merely relocated. Mutation: applying it fails `WorkerContextHygieneTest`'s "clean after a job that THREW" **and only that test**. **(2) §D4 must SAVE/RESTORE, not flush.** Under `QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync` — every CI job — `SyncQueue` raises both events **inline in the caller's stack**, so a blind flush wipes the ambient request context mid-request. A LIFO stack in a `private static` (load-bearing: `Dispatcher::createClassCallable` resolves a **fresh listener per dispatch**, so instance state would silently degrade back into a flush) is correct under both a worker (saved value null ⇒ restore *is* flush) and sync. Deliberately **NOT** gated on `connectionName !== 'sync'` — that gate would make the listener **dead code in every CI job**, i.e. exactly the unverifiability ADR-0007 was written to end. Mutation: a blind flush fails precisely the two sync tests and no worker test. **(3) §D7's `$tries = 3` INVERTS §D9.** `RateLimited` enforces its ceiling with `$job->release()`, and `DatabaseQueue::release()` (`:328`) re-pushes preserving the **already-incremented** `attempts` — so three fairness *deferrals* land the job in `failed_jobs`, converting "this tenant is throttled" into "this tenant's jobs permanently failed". `TenantAwareJob` therefore declares **no `$tries` at all**: `retryUntil()` (time-based, blind to releases) + `$maxExceptions = 3`. Mutation is instructive — adding `$tries = 3` *while keeping* `retryUntil()` changes **nothing** (a non-null `retryUntil` makes `maxTries` dead code in the worker), so the test kills the ADR-as-written combination (`$tries` **without** `retryUntil`) and the code comment says so rather than overclaiming. **(4) §D6's "every job MUST declare `$queue`" is a FATAL ERROR as written.** `Illuminate\Bus\Queueable:29` declares `public $queue;` **untyped**; redeclaring it with a different initial value fatals any class using the trait. Replaced by the framework's `#[Queue(QueueName::X)]` attribute — which takes a `UnitEnum`, is read first by `Dispatcher::pushCommandToQueue()`, **is inherited from a parent** (`ReadsClassAttributes::getAttributeInstance` walks `getParentClass()` in a do/while, so `MaintenanceJob` names its queue once for every sweep), and is *more* statically checkable than a string literal. **(5) §D13's status comparison would have taken the whole queue down.** `tenants.status` is a stancl virtual-column attribute **explicitly not cast** — a plain `?string` — so `$tenant->status !== TenantStatus::Active` compares string to **enum object**, is **always true**, and would release-then-delete **every job for every tenant on the platform**: a silent total outage no existing test would catch. Fixed structurally with `Tenant::isActive()` + `scopeActive()` (comparing `->value`/`tryFrom()`, matching `SuperAdminService`), so §D3's fan-out and §D13's guard share **one** definition; `JobContractTest` additionally pins `'status'` in `getCustomColumns()`, because removing it silently relocates the value into the `data` json column and the predicate then matches **nothing**. **Two feared regressions were REFUTED before a line was written and confirmed after:** the `after_commit => true` flip and the flush listener break **zero** existing tests — the only dispatch site (`AttachmentStorageService:82`) is reached by no un-faked test (`G6FieldTypesTest:49` is `Queue::fake()`; `:254` calls `->handle()` directly). Reassuring for the diff, damning for the status quo: it confirms the substrate was exercised by **nothing**, so the new integration test carries all the weight. **The enforcement is three independent layers**, per user decision to bump `composer.json` `"php"` `^8.3 → ^8.4` (every real environment was already 8.4; only the manifest lagged): a **PHP 8.4 abstract property hook** (`abstract public string $tenantId { get; }` — a job that forgets it is a **class-load fatal**, verified), the **runtime uuid assertion** in `final handle()` (which also names the all-zeroes `BelongsToTenant` sentinel separately, since a job carrying it serialized an *absent* tenant — a different bug from a malformed one), and **`scripts/job-payload-lint.php`**. `handle()`/`middleware()`/`failed()`/`retryUntil()` are all `final` because an override loses the assertion, `applyLocal`, the transaction or the §D9 limiter **with no runtime symptom on a warm worker**; extension goes through `handleForTenant()`/`jobMiddleware()`/`failureContext()`/`retryWindowHours()`. `$deleteWhenMissingModels` is `final false`, sealing §D5's named trap. **The linter departs from its two siblings in two documented ways:** it is **two-pass** (`NameResolver` resolves names but not ancestry, so pass 1 builds an FQCN→parent map; a parent resolving outside `app/` fails **loudly** rather than passing silently — the H3 queued-mailable case needs a decision, not a default) and it **never uses `->getLast()`** (unlike `migration-lint.php:146/:192`), so a shadow-named `TenantAwareJob` in another namespace cannot pass — **verified red**. Its §D5 rule is **inverted into a closed scalar whitelist** rather than a model detector, because "is this an Eloquent model" is **undecidable** from a type declaration: `SerializesAndRestoresModelIdentifiers` branches on the *runtime value* and `SerializesModels::__serialize` reflects over every non-static property, so `mixed`/untyped/`object` all reach `restoreModel()` invisibly. **Red-then-green proven per rule** (5 violations in one fixture, each with file:line + remediation), and it is wired into **BOTH** `composer.json`'s `quality` array **and a new `ci.yml` step** — mandatory, because **no CI job runs `composer run quality`**; `static-analysis` invokes the four scripts individually, so a composer-only registration would have gated nothing. **Verification went beyond the suite:** a genuine **two-process** run (dispatch in one container process, drain in a separate `queue:work`) took a real attachment `pending → skipped` — the path the in-process test structurally cannot cover — and then the **compose `worker` service** did the same unattended. That exercise found a real config defect the tests could not: `php:8.4-fpm-alpine` ships **no php.ini**, so the CLI `memory_limit` is exactly **128M**, and `queue:work`'s default `--memory=128` means the graceful over-budget recycle can *never* fire before PHP's hard limit does — turning a clean restart into a fatal OOM mid-job. Fixed with `--memory=112`. **`default` is deliberately ABSENT from the worker's `--queue=` ordering**: a job that escaped the linter should strand visibly (`select queue, count(*) from jobs group by 1`), not be silently rescued by the very worker whose gate it evaded. **Forbidden connections DELETED, not annotated** (user decision): `deferred`/`background`/`failover` are gone from `config/queue.php`, so `QUEUE_CONNECTION=deferred` now throws `InvalidArgumentException` loudly at boot — a gate rather than one more piece of prose-as-gate, which is the pattern ADR-0007 §Context indicts. `failover` had to go regardless since it referenced `deferred`. **Gates: Pest 1045 (+44)** across 7 new files in `tests/Feature/Queue/`; **PHPStan level 8 ZERO errors on every H2 file** (the 77 app-wide are the documented local baseline — `E2eSeeder.php` is untouched by H2); Pint green; `schedule:list` confirms `10 3 * * *`. **A PHPStan finding was a real bug, not noise:** it flagged `$job instanceof MaintenanceJob` as always-false inside a branch already narrowed to `TenantAwareJob` — dead code, since the two are unrelated classes and the null check already covered it. Narrowings recorded rather than papered over: `$timeout = 60` is **unverifiable in CI** (SIGALRM is armed only in `daemon()`, never under `--once`); the genuine §D8 **two-process race** is not reproducible in-process (the *ordering contract* is fully covered, the race is not — no committing-test precedent); `MaintenanceJob`'s **fan-out arm has no production caller** until the first rollup vertical, only `activeTenants()` tests; fairness buckets, overlap locks, the schedule mutex and `jobs` itself all contend on **one Postgres instance**; and `RateLimited` stores `md5($limiterName.$limit->key)`, so fairness buckets are **not greppable** by tenant in the cache table.
- **H1a (as-built)** — Phase 3's entry point: a **docs-only PR** carrying **ADR-0007 (async execution substrate)** + twelve document reconciliations, on the G5a/ADR-0006 precedent (PR #32 `d2a3ff7`). **The premise was that Phase 3 needs an async contract before code; the audit found the foundation is almost entirely prose.** Exactly one queued job exists (`ScanAttachmentJob`, `final`, defining **none** of `$queue`/`$tries`/`$backoff`/`$timeout`/`failed()`/`middleware()`); **nothing consumes the queue** (no worker or scheduler compose service; the only committed worker invocation is `queue:listen` in `composer.json`'s `dev` script); **the scheduler does not exist** (`routes/console.php` is 8 stock lines, no `withSchedule`, no `app/Console/`) while **four documents assert one** — `feature-backlog.md:85` said outright *"scheduler + email + async export already exists"*; and `onQueue(` has **zero hits** against a five-name catalog documented as binding in two places. **The keystone finding is a live defect two documents called "Mitigated":** `TenantContext::$tenantId` is a **process-lifetime PHP static** that `applyLocal()` never rolls back (it scopes only the DB GUC to the transaction), and there is **no `Queue::before`/`JobProcessing` listener anywhere** — so on a long-lived worker the GUC goes NULL while the static still holds the last tenant, and `BelongsToTenant` then injects it into the next job's reads and `creating` fill. RLS still fails closed (so no cross-tenant *disclosure* — reads return zero rows, inserts throw), but ADR-0002:125 and security-threat-model:40 both promised *"fails fast (explicit exception)"* and **it did not**; it survived only because no second job type exists. **ADR-0007 is `D1…D13`** and, per user decision, **deliberately departs from ADR-0006's skeleton by carrying no weighted scorecard** — that ADR scored a *spike* with measurements; this one has none, and §D9's ceilings are explicitly unvalidated assumptions, so a rubric would manufacture false precision. It uses ADR-0005's plain drivers + Concern/Choice table with ADR-0006's `**DN — …**` bullets. Substance: **D1** `database` driver on Postgres + plain `queue:work`, **superseding ADR-0005 rows 27–28 in part** (Redis/Memurai + Horizon) — the first *row-level* supersession in the repo, chosen over amendment because partial supersession is the honest description and avoids retiring a live ADR; **D2** `TenantAwareJob` (uuid assertion — the "fails fast" ADR-0002 §D6 promised — + `DB::transaction`/`applyLocal` + the `setPermissionsTeamId()` the HTTP middleware sets and **no job does**, without which any job calling `hasPermissionTo()` fails closed); **D3** `MaintenanceJob` for cross-tenant work, justified structurally — a cross-tenant transaction is **not expressible**, since the GUC is a scalar and `TenantIsolation::tenantMatch()` is flat equality with no set/any-tenant mode; **D4** the flush listener that makes those two docs true; **D5** scalar-ids-only (`SerializesModels::__unserialize` runs in `CallQueuedHandler::call` **before** `handle()` under a NULL GUC, so a model payload is a permanent failure) **with the `$deleteWhenMissingModels` trap named** so nobody "fixes" it into silent data loss; **D6** the five queue names now binding; **D7** `$tries`/backoff + `retry_after` **90→120** so `timeout < retry_after`; **D8** `after_commit => true` — **decided here, implemented in H2** — closing a real bug where `AttachmentStorageService:82` dispatches outside any transaction so a worker can beat the row and strand `virus_scan_status` at `pending` **forever**, structurally untestable under `sync` i.e. under every current CI job; **D9** the per-tenant job-rate ceiling that **closes R6**; **D10** no new tables (a `tenant_id`-bearing one trips migration-lint, and both escapes — RLS in the reservation hot path, or an exempt table holding tenant ids — are worse); **D11** `deferred`/`background`/`failover` forbidden for tenant work (under `deferred` the HTTP session GUC is still live, making a correct job and a free-riding one **indistinguishable in testing**); **D12** structured `failed()` + the never-stated constraint that any tenant-facing failure UI is a **cross-tenant read of an RLS-free table**; **D13** tenant-lifecycle handling + the explicit non-goal that `tenants.status` is read by **no** middleware/policy/RLS predicate today. **Verification caught six citation defects in the source plan before they were written** (three Explore agents, every `file:line` re-read against source): `handle()` is a `function (): void {}` closure not `fn() =>` (syntactically impossible for a statement list); "no guzzle/no Redis" was false (guzzle is transitive at `composer.lock:802`, Redis exists in infra — narrowed to *no first-party call site* / *no Redis-backed queue*); **`horizon:terminate` is not in `deploy.ps1` at all** (docs-only claim, so that correction stands but inverted); migration-lint Rule 1 is `:105-117` not `:99`; `TenantInvitationNotification` interpolates at `:33-35` not `:44`; and the webhook retry ladder is at §1 `:13`, not §4 `:49-61` — so the unbuilt banner was retargeted to the doc head. **Two H-map claims were REFUTED/downgraded and deliberately NOT written:** the *"RBAC docs say 27 permissions"* correction is **wrong** (§5 already enumerates 28 and names `scopes.manage` as the 28th; §3's "fixed catalog" refers to the five **roles**) — writing it would have *introduced* an error, so the R6 dangling-pointer fix was substituted as the tenth reconciliation; and *"PRD lists 8 roadmap items"* is unfounded (the 12 is verbatim at `PRD.md:405`; the 8 came from this tracker). **Two extra defects found during verification were folded in** (user-approved): ADR-0002:76's dangling `[D7]` anchor → `[D6]`, and technical-architecture §5 layer 5, which described a "job middleware" that was never built. Ships **docs-only** — no product code, no migration, no `ci.yml` change.
- Phase 2 = **Increment G (G1→G11) — ✅ COMPLETE, all eleven merged.** G1→G6 MERGED; G7 (XLSForm) COMPLETE; G8 (PWA/offline) COMPLETE; G9 COMPLETE (G9a PR #42 + #43, G9b PR #44 `eb6bda7`); G10 COMPLETE (G10a #45, G10b1 #46, G10b2 #47); **G11 MERGED (PR #48 `506ff97`, all 6 CI jobs green)**. With it, **Increment G and Phase 2 closed.**
- **G11 (as-built)** — richer personalization: accent / text-size / dyslexia-friendly font (PRD Feature #9 Phase 2, DSR §2.9, data-dictionary §19). **The starting premise in this tracker was wrong and is corrected below: the columns did NOT exist.** The only migration for `user_ui_preferences` was B1's, which shipped `theme_mode` alone; `accent` was a **hardcoded `'blueprint'` literal** in `User::uiTheme()` that had never touched the database. So G11 *is* a schema increment — new migration `2026_07_21_000002` adds `accent_token varchar(30) NULL` / `font_size_scale varchar(15) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'standard'` / `use_dyslexia_friendly_font boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`, matching §19 byte-for-byte, with **no RLS change** (the belongs-to-user policy set is row-level, so it gates rows not columns). **Three new enums** (`ThemeMode`, `FontSizeScale` — both catalogued in §19 since Increment C but never written — plus `AccentToken`, which **is** the §19 application-layer whitelist since that column deliberately has no CHECK). **The keystone finding: the shipped `[data-accent='teal']` block was broken in four ways and nobody could have seen it** — `-bg-hover` pointed at `--mds-primary-700` (a *blue* hover on a teal button), `-bg-active`/`-tint` were never overridden, and there was **no dark variant at all**; since `[data-accent]` carries the same specificity as `[data-theme-mode='dark']` and sat later in source order, teal won in dark and painted light `#1B5E5E` on the `#123350` ground — **1.74:1** for both `action-primary-fg` and the focus ring, failing WCAG 1.4.3 and 1.4.11. It survived two increments because **nothing in the product could set `data-accent` and no test had ever set it**. Fixed by extending `accent-teal` from one step to a **7-step ramp** (50/300/400/500/600/700/800; `600` unchanged, it is ratified) with **all 17 pairings independently computed and verified** — teal is never worse than Blueprint at the equivalent role and is *better* in dark (fill 6.68 vs 6.14, hover 4.82 vs Blueprint's failing 3.96). **The dark+teal payload is defined ONCE** as `--mds-_accent-teal-dark-*` private customs that both the explicit-opt-in selector and the `prefers-color-scheme` twin assign from — the existing neutral dark block is already copy-pasted across those two sites, and a third copy-paste was the obvious future divergence. **The docs' type-scale rule could not ship as written:** §2.9 specified "+2px per level, never changing line-heights", which at extra_large yields `body-sm` as **17px text in an 18px line box (ratio 1.06)** and `caption` 16px-in-16px (1.00) — clipping descenders and failing WCAG 1.4.12, i.e. an accessibility feature shipping an accessibility regression. Replaced (user decision) with **proportional ×1.125/×1.25 scaling of BOTH font-size and line-height**, font-size rounded then line-height **derived** as `round(roundedFontSize × the role's original ratio)` — independent rounding would compress `caption` from 1.333→1.286. Every role now holds within ±2%, floor **1.220**; §2.9 corrected with the authoritative 11×2 table. `code` **is** size-scaled but **not** face-swapped — a deliberate asymmetry (size is a low-vision accommodation and `code` is the smallest role; the face swap is letterform disambiguation for prose, where mono's column alignment would suffer). **OpenDyslexic is vendored** (5.2.5 latin, SIL OFL 1.1, licence verbatim per OFL §2) — the system's first webfont, but **zero-cost by construction**: a browser fetches a `@font-face` src only when a rule using the family matches, and the only such rule is the attribute-gated one, so a user who never opts in downloads **zero font bytes**. The `@font-face` lives in a **new `fonts.css` imported only by the admin app** — `theme-overrides.css` would have shipped it to the guest bundle, since `public-runtime.css` imports that file. **The reflow risk was much smaller than it looked**: `AppLayout`'s `.app-shell__content` is `overflow-y: auto`, which per CSS Overflow makes the other axis `auto` too — so it is its own scroll container and page content never reaches the document's overflow chain that `assertClean` measures. Only `TopNav` was exposed (~344/375px at extra_large, ~31px headroom — one long tenant name from failing), hardened with `min-width: 0` + ellipsis plus an `overflow-x: clip` belt on `.app-shell` (`clip`, not `hidden`: creates no scroll container, does not break `position: sticky`). **Exactly ONE touch to `packages/design-system/src/components/**`, and it is a real bug fix rather than an API change** (see the `MdsDataTable` finding below) — the accent picker is a label-only `MdsSegmentedControl` (a colour swatch would be a colour-ONLY signifier per WCAG 1.4.1, and the control already previews the accent for free since its selected chip is painted with `--mds-color-action-primary-bg`), and the dyslexia toggle reuses `MdsCheckbox` rather than building the specified-but-unbuilt `MdsSwitch` (DSR §3.2 requires a switch carry visible text anyway — i.e. a checkbox with extra steps). That keeps the DSR §1.2 governance gate and the flaky `design-system-a11y` job out of the diff. **`ThemeQuickToggle.vue` diff is literally zero lines**: `useTheme.ts` keeps `useThemePreference()` at its exact C2 signature as a mode-only facade over the new `useAppearancePreference()`. **The anti-clobber guarantee is server-side, not client-side** — every rule on the new `UpdateAppearanceRequest` is `sometimes`, so an absent key is never validated and never reaches `updateOrCreate`; even a stale client cannot wipe an axis it doesn't know about. **Verified by mutation** (making one column write unconditional fails the partial-PATCH test exactly where expected). **Four new guard tests make the hand-authored CSS mechanically verifiable**: `type-scale` re-derives all 44 declarations from the token JSON, `theme-overrides` asserts the duplicated dark blocks are identical (catching the *pre-existing* neutral copy-paste risk too), `token-references` resolves every `var(--mds-*)` in the tree, and `useTheme` pins the "default = ABSENCE of the attribute" convention. **The dead-token sweep found 16 undefined tokens across 10 files, not the 4+ sites PROGRESS estimated** — and it was load-bearing, not cosmetic: `--mds-font-size-body`/`-caption` and `--mds-type-heading-sm-*` had no fallback, so those declarations were invalid at computed-value time and inherited instead, meaning they would have scaled by inheritance rather than by their type role under `data-font-size`. Sites *with* a fallback were collapsed to that fallback (behaviour-preserving) rather than re-pointed, since changing them is a design decision, not a cleanup. **Pest 1001 (+13)**; Pint / controller-gate / migration-lint green; **PHPStan 0 errors on every G11 file**; vue-tsc clean; no `openapi.json` drift (zero API routes — preferences are Inertia web routes). **The E2E found a real bug that no unit test could have, exactly as in G10a — and it was in `MdsDataTable`, not in G11's own code.** At 834px, `extra_large` + the dyslexia face (each harmless alone; only the *combination* triggered it) made the page gain **50px of genuine horizontal scroll** — `window.scrollTo(500,0)` really moved it, so not a `scrollWidth` artifact. Diagnosis mattered more than the fix: `.app-shell`'s `overflow-x: clip` belt made **no difference at all** (identical with `visible`/`hidden`), `body.scrollWidth` was a clean 834 while only `html.scrollWidth` read 884, and every overflowing element was correctly inside the table's `overflow-x: auto` wrapper. The culprit was `.mds-table__sr` — the visually-hidden "Actions" label — which is `position: absolute` while `.mds-table__scroll` was `position: static`, so its containing block resolved **outside** the scroll wrapper and the wrapper could not clip it; a 1px span past the last column then extended the *document's* scrollable width. **No `overflow-x` on any ancestor can fix that**, which is why the belt was useless here: an absolutely positioned element is clipped by its containing block, not by an arbitrary scrolling ancestor. One-line fix (`position: relative` on `.mds-table__scroll`) — a latent DataTable bug that personalization merely made reachable by widening the table, so fixed at source rather than worked around per-page. This is the **only** touch to `src/components/**`, and it satisfies the DSR §1.2 governance gate because the DSR is updated in the same commit. New `personalization-axe` spec is **18 runs, not a 72-run matrix**: extra_large strictly dominates large for reflow and dark+teal is the only genuinely new colour surface, so Loop A scans accent contrast in both themes and Loop B scans only the maximum-stress combination. Narrowings: no UI-interaction E2E (it would persist preferences for the shared storageState user and silently re-tint every later spec under `workers: 1` — persistence is covered by Pest instead); personalization remains authenticated-app-only by design; `MdsSwitch` still unbuilt; Blueprint's own dark `bg-active` measures **2.52:1** with white text — pre-existing, invisible to axe (which never evaluates `:active`), recorded in exceptions-log #6 rather than fixed, to keep the diff to its subject.
- **G10b2 (as-built)** — the scoping hierarchy UI: the surface that finally makes the Reviewer role assignable by a human. **Adds no new authorization logic** — the plan was deliberately shaped to keep that literally true, so the form-scope gate is stacked middleware (`can:update,form` + `can:viewAny,ScopeNode`) rather than a new `FormPolicy::assignScope` method; `ScopeNodePolicy::viewAny` **is** `scopes.manage`, so the two are behaviourally identical and the smaller diff wins. **Transport is forced, not stylistic:** `bootstrap/app.php`'s `$isApi` keys on the `api/v1/*` **path**, and Laravel runs custom render callbacks (`Handler::render():718`) **before** JSON negotiation — so a `ScopeNodeException` on a web route returns `back()->with('toast')`, a 302, **even to an XHR**. `builderClient` would see `response.ok`, skip its guarded branch, and throw a raw `SyntaxError` parsing HTML. Hence: **every mutation is an Inertia visit; the only fetches are two read-only sidecars** (`/scopes/{node}/impact`, `/scopes/{node}/grants`), which raise no domain exception and negotiate 403/404 to JSON cleanly. **`ScopeTree.vue` is the app's first tree widget** (no design-system primitive; there was not one other `role="tree"` in the repo, so every decision here is precedent). Flat `<ul role="tree">` → `<li role="treeitem">` with explicit `aria-level`/`setsize`/`posinset` — valid because `tree.requiredOwned = ['group','treeitem']`, and chosen because visibility, sibling sets and ancestor walks then collapse to one linear pass over the `COLLATE "C"` path order. **The merge-blocker, which neither the design pass nor the judge caught and an adversarial critic did:** `getOwnedRoles` (axe.js:27380) pushes any child carrying a role, a **global `aria-*` attribute**, or focusability as an *owned* child rather than recursing past it, and anything outside `['group','treeitem']` then fails `aria-required-children` (critical, wcag2a) — so the assertive live region and the `MdsEmptyState` are **siblings** of the `<ul>`, and the axe scan targets `.scopes__pane`, not PROGRESS's originally-specified `.scopes__tree`. Roving tabindex runs on a **local `activeId` kept distinct from the server-owned selection**; selection does **not** follow focus (arrow-stepping must not fire the detail panel's sidecar). Row actions live in the detail panel so the grip is the row's only focusable descendant — not because `nested-interactive` would fire (verified against axe source: its matcher keys on `childrenPresentational`, which `treeitem` lacks) but because four buttons per row explodes the tab order and pollutes every row's name-from-contents. **`useScopeTreeMove` is a deliberate SIBLING of `useCanvasReorder`, not a reuse** (that one is typed to `BuilderStore`): it picks a **parent, never a sibling index** — `move()` takes no index, so before/after drop zones are unimplementable — mutates nothing, and confirms, because a move can be refused. No-live-preview is an **a11y** property too: the DOM never reorders mid-grab, so the focused grip cannot be unmounted under the user. **Two real bugs the E2E found:** (1) grab-mode entered from the detail panel's "Move…" focuses the *row*, whose keydown was doing tree navigation — fixed by delegating row keys to the move handler while grabbed; (2) the outcome was announced from the visit's `onSuccess`, but a **no-op or refused** move returns props identical to what is rendered, so a reference watcher never fires — leaving the announcement silent **and the tree stuck in grab mode**. Settled from the refreshed props with an `onFinish` backstop; `settleIfPending` is idempotent so whichever signal lands first wins. **The form→node picker is its own route** (user decision: require `scopes.manage`): writing `scope_node_id` confers capacity on the form **and, through `SubmissionPolicy::collaboratesWith`, its entire submission history** to every holder of a grant on that node and any `includes_descendants` ancestor — and a plain `form_editor` passes `can:update,form` on any form they created (`FormService::create` mints them the editor grant). The column **is** in `Form::$fillable`, so the write is centralised in an explicit `forceFill` (`FormService::assignScope`) and a test pins that `PATCH /forms/{form}` cannot set it. **Presenter discipline:** two grouped aggregates, never `nodeReach()` per row (a prefix-LIKE per node against a hierarchy the resolver sizes at ~44k); `form_count` counts `withTrashed()` to agree with the impact modal opened from it. **Recipients are correct by construction, not by filtering** — the `users_visibility` RLS policy already admits only ACTIVE co-tenants plus self, so an invited member is a **404, not the `grant_recipient_inactive` toast** (`ResourceGrantServiceTest:113` says as much: RLS gets there first, the service guard is defence in depth) — the test asserts the real failure rather than encoding a fiction. Capacities render **disabled-with-reason, not hidden** (unreachable under today's 5-role matrix; forward-looking). **Pest 988 (+22)**; Vitest **414 unchanged**; Pint / controller-gate / migration-lint green; PHPStan **0 errors on all G10b2 files**; vue-tsc clean; **no `openapi.json` drift** (tenant-web routes are outside the surface). New `scopes-axe` spec **24/24 across all three viewports**, plus `/scopes` in `responsive-axe` (6/6). `E2eSeeder` gains a **5-level** hierarchy (deep enough that the 375px overflow case is actually reachable — a shallow fixture would make `responsive-axe` a false negative), forms at differing depths, a deactivated branch, a second **ACTIVE** member, and a descendant-inclusive reviewer grant. Narrowing: tree payload capped at 2,000 nodes with an honest notice (expand-on-demand is the follow-up); grants managed per node only.
- **G10b1 (as-built)** — the increment that makes the Reviewer role assignable. **Four decisions taken with the user up front:** one node per form (keep the `forms.scope_node_id` pointer, no pivot); fix the over-broad form list in this increment; **one** new `manage:scopes` ability mapped to both `scopes.manage` and `forms.collaborators.manage`; split G10b into backend (G10b1) + UI (G10b2). **`ScopeNodeService` gains `update`/`setActive`/`delete`/`move`/`deletionImpact`.** The keystone is **`move()`**: PROGRESS previously specified `FOR UPDATE` on node + target parent, which is **necessary but NOT sufficient** — a concurrent move of an *ancestor of the target* re-paths the target without locking it, so the first mover grafts its subtree onto a stale prefix, and `path` is exactly what authorization prefix-matches. Resolved with a **transaction-scoped advisory lock keyed on the tenant** (`pg_advisory_xact_lock(class, crc32(tenant))` — the two-int form, deliberately not the undocumented internal `hashtext`; the `_xact_` variant so a crashed request cannot strand it). It is the **only advisory lock in the codebase** (every other service serializes on a row) because it is the only operation whose correctness spans an unbounded row set. The `FOR UPDATE` re-reads stay and remain load-bearing (authoritative post-lock rows + blocking concurrent rename/deactivate). Then: cycle check as ONE self-inclusive prefix test (also covers move-onto-self, and is now the **only** thing preventing a longer cycle — `scope_nodes_no_self_parent` only ever covered the single-node case, so that migration's comment was corrected); depth cap measured across the **whole subtree** (a shallow node can carry a deep one); and a **single** `UPDATE` re-path over the constant-prefix `LIKE` (atomic, index-served by `(tenant_id, path)` under `COLLATE "C"`, one statement regardless of subtree size). **`ScopeNode::booted()` is KEPT VERBATIM, not relaxed** — the re-path is a query-builder statement so it fires no model events, meaning the guard still covers every ordinary save while the one audited writer sits behind the locks; an `unguarded`/re-entrancy flag was rejected as something a future caller can switch off. **A real PostgreSQL trap found in testing:** `substring(path from ?)` with an untyped bind resolves to the POSIX-**regex** overload `substring(text, text)` and returns NULL on no match — it would have nulled `path` on every touched row. Caught by NOT NULL; fixed to `substr(path, ?::int)` with both numeric binds cast explicitly. **New migration `2026_07_21_000001`** adds two CHECKs that make an incorrectly re-pathed row impossible *regardless of writer* (Eloquent, builder, raw SQL, a future migration): `scope_nodes_path_self_suffix_chk` (a path ends with its own id) and `scope_nodes_depth_matches_path_chk` (`depth` = path segment count, i.e. slashes − 2 — which also forces `path` and `depth` to be written in the same statement). **Node deletion now removes the subtree's grants in-transaction** — `resource_grants` is a morph with no FK, so nothing cascaded them and every delete silently manufactured orphaned authorization rows (this is cleanup at the creating site, *not* the deferred orphan sweeper), via a SUBQUERY not a `whereIn` (PG caps binds at 65535). **New `ResourceGrantService`** (grant/revoke; upserts so a demotion **replaces** rather than accumulates, per the unique key that deliberately excludes `capacity`; locks the re-resolved tenant-scoped target so concurrent grants cannot 23505-race; `->scopeable()->associate()` never mass-assignment) and **`ResourceGrantPolicy`** (registered explicitly — an unmapped model class fails **open**) with the escalation rules: base `forms.collaborators.manage`, **no self-grant**, and **anti-amplification** via the new `ResourceCapacity::anyPermission()` (editor→`forms.edit.any`, reviewer→`submissions.review.any`). Rule 3 is **unreachable under the shipped 5-role matrix** and is documented + tested against raw permission subsets rather than seeded roles, precisely so it is not filed as dead code the way `forms.collaborators.manage` itself was. **`ResourceGrantResolver::nodeReach()`** is the blast-radius counter, added *there* (not a parallel query) so the preview and the grant cannot disagree — it returns `{direct, descendant}`, reports **zero for a deactivated node or one under an inactive branch** (a preview advertising access the resolver will refuse is a lie an admin escalates on), and counts through the same `withTrashed()` scope the resolver uses. `escapeLike()` made public so the service shares one escaping rule. **`forget()` discipline documented + tested per writer** — the per-user variant clears ONLY `$sets`, leaving `$formPaths`/`$inactive` stale, so `move`/`setActive`/`delete` must all call the **argument-less** `forget()`. **The form-list leak was fixed on BOTH surfaces:** `FormPresenter::list()` *and* `GET /api/v1/forms` (`FormApiController::index`) had the identical "every non-archived tenant form to anyone passing the read gate" behaviour — fixing only the presenter would have moved the leak to the API rather than closed it; scoped via `grantedFormIdsQuery($user, Editor)` (Editor specifically: it is the authoring list). **API:** `manage:scopes` + 6 new paths (`/scopes`, `/scopes/{scopeNode}`, `/scopes/{scopeNode}/move` — deliberately separate from PATCH since it is a locked op with its own refusals — `/scopes/{scopeNode}/impact`, `/resource-grants`, `/resource-grants/{resourceGrant}`). **Every route pairs `ability:` with a `can:` policy gate**, which is what makes the single coarse ability safe (the map's any-of semantics would otherwise let a `scopes.manage`-only principal reach the grant routes) — recorded in `ApiAbilities::MANAGE_SCOPES` and api-spec §2.6 as a constraint on future routes. **Pest 966 (+64)**; Pint/controller-gate/migration-lint green; Larastan **0 errors** on all G10b files; vue-tsc green; `openapi.json` regenerated (23 paths), Redocly-valid, **no drift**. **The end-to-end walkthrough was run and all 18 checks passed** (4-level tree → grant on an interior node with descendants → move the subtree → deactivate an intermediate node → escalation refusals → deletion impact) — the exercise that, in G10a, found the bug the tests missed. Ships **backend-only**: no routes in `tenant.php`, no Vue, no Playwright (all G10b2).
- **G10a (as-built)** — Generalized `morphTo` resource-scoping, backend only. **G10 had NO design spec** — one roadmap bullet repeated in 5 places; the whole written contract is PRD §6 ("a generalized `morphTo`-based resource-scoping mechanism, the clean successor to the legacy PSGC/catchment-area hack"), PRD §7 (never a hardcoded geography table or a PHP switch-on-a-level-column; tenants model their own reference data), architecture §5 row 11 (`*_type` + `*_id`, resolved by the framework), and RBAC §8:215 nominating `form_collaborators`' two-layer composition as "the general pattern for any future resource that needs per-instance scoping beyond the tenant level". **Unified reading chosen with the user:** two tables. **`scope_nodes`** = a tenant-defined hierarchy with ZERO platform semantics (`name`/`code`/`node_type` are the tenant's own labels, never switched on) — adjacency list + a self-inclusive materialized `path` **`COLLATE "C"`** (load-bearing: descendant resolution is a constant-prefix `LIKE`, which PG compiles into indexable range quals only under C), depth CHECK 0–12, `is_active` instead of a `deleted_at` (a soft-delete the resolver must remember to filter is an authorization landmine), **composite** self-FK `(tenant_id, parent_id)` per ADR-0002 §D5 because **PG runs referential actions BYPASSING RLS**. **`resource_grants`** = the polymorphic grant (`scopeable` → `form` | `scope_node`, the repo's 2nd real `morphTo`; `Relation::morphMap` NOT `enforceMorphMap`), unique on `(tenant_id, scopeable_type, scopeable_id, user_id)` with **capacity deliberately NOT in the key** so a demotion replaces rather than adds, per-grant `includes_descendants` DEFAULT FALSE. `forms` gains `scope_node_id` (composite FK + PG15 **column-list** `SET NULL (scope_node_id)` — a plain composite SET NULL would null `tenant_id` and violate NOT NULL). **The security keystone: a morph has no FK, so under plain `strict` RLS an INSERT with my own `tenant_id` + another tenant's form id is ACCEPTED by Postgres** (verified: `strictSql()` emits only `WITH CHECK (tenant_id = ctx)`) — and unlike `attachments` that row is an authorization *decision input*. New **`TenantIsolation::resourceGrantGuard`** (6th variant, a new *instance* of the shipped `draftChildGuard` shape) adds a per-alias same-tenant `EXISTS` to INSERT/UPDATE `WITH CHECK`; SELECT/DELETE stay tenant-only so an orphaned grant stays revokable; **must be the SOLE write policy per command** (PG OR-combines same-command permissive policies — also calling `withTenantIsolation()` would silently restore bare tenant equality *and still pass CI*, so `TenantIsolationSqlTest` asserts exactly-one-policy-per-command). **`ResourceGrantResolver`** (`scoped()`, not `singleton()`) is the single interpreter of `resource_grants`, answering both `holds()` and the list twin `grantedFormIdsQuery()` from one grant set so policy and inbox cannot diverge; memo key is **(user, tenant)** — a user-only key bleeds across `enterTenant()` calls and makes authorization tests pass for the wrong reason. Resolution runs **downward from the grant**, never upward with a leading `%` (unindexable, and it sits in the inbox query); bounded by grant count, never descendant count (PG caps binds at 65535; a PSGC region is ~44k nodes). `withTrashed()` throughout is **behaviour preservation** — the old `FormCollaborator` subquery never joined `forms`, so a grant-holder always still saw soft-deleted forms' submissions. **Backfill**: runs on `pgsql_privileged` with `withinTransaction = false`, because migrations run as `meridian_app` with no tenant GUC → under FORCE RLS a naive `INSERT…SELECT` **reads nothing, writes nothing, throws nothing**, and the next migration would then drop the only copy of every access grant (a silent authorization wipe on a green log). Reuses `fc.id` as the grant PK (idempotent re-run; keeps UUIDv7 ordering), guards with `<` not `!=` (re-runs pass; `0<0` false so `migrate:fresh` passes), plus a post-flight cross-tenant re-check because the privileged connection *bypassed* the guard. **`form_collaborators` dropped**; its create-migration deliberately KEPT (`migrate:fresh` replays in order). **Adds `scopes.manage` — a 28th permission**, changing RBAC §3/§5's documented "fixed catalog of 27": reusing `tenant.settings.manage` would be actively harmful since `ApiAbilities` maps `manage:settings` onto it, retroactively widening every already-minted token. **One deliberate behaviour change:** `SubmissionPolicy::create` (manual encoding) now requires **Editor** capacity, not either — at subtree scale a reviewer grant on an interior node would otherwise confer write access to every form beneath it. Everything else is behaviour-identical **by construction**: after backfill every grant targets a form, every `scope_node_id` is NULL, and G10a ships no writer for either, so the node branch is a constant-false conjunct — **the pre-existing suite is the regression gate, and it passed unchanged**. **Found by the END-TO-END walkthrough, not by the tests** (which is why the plan required driving a real hierarchy through the resolver): deactivating an **intermediate** node did not cut off its descendants, because `is_active` was only checked on the granted node and the form's own node — making it a control that *looks* like it revokes a branch but doesn't, i.e. exactly the landmine the no-`deleted_at` decision exists to prevent. Fixed by loading the tenant's inactive paths once and reusing the same prefix machinery, applied to **both** query shapes (+2 tests). **Pest 902 (+84)**; Larastan 78 errors = exact `main` baseline with **zero in G10a files**; Pint/migration-lint/controller-gate/vue-tsc green; **no `openapi.json` drift** (zero routes). Ships **backend-only** — no routes, controllers, or UI. **All 6 CI jobs green on the FIRST push** (G9a and G9b each needed 3 follow-up fixes).

On a successful resubmit the old conflict row is discarded (`discardConflict`); a "discard this response" hatch also exists. `RuntimeSession` gains a `resolving` mode that **suppresses autosave** (new `enabled` guard on `useAutosave` — the durable copy is the outbox row, so a transient review can't clobber a live `[form_version_id+slug]` draft) and hides `SyncStatus`. New outbox helpers: `listConflicts(slug)`, `nextConflict()`/`discardConflict()` on `useSyncOutbox` (interactive resolution is **current-form-slug-scoped** — App's single share-token client is bound to `bootstrap.slug`; the global conflict count may exceed what "Review" acts on). `conflict_code` on `OutboxRow` records which 409 parked it (non-indexed → **no Dexie version bump**). **Backend (content-checksum 409):** new nullable `submission_answers.answers_content_checksum` + `AnswersContentChecksum` (canonical SHA-256, key-sorted, list-order-preserving). `SubmissionPipeline` hashes the **normalized** answers; on a duplicate `client_submission_uuid` it compares stored-vs-incoming — match (or a legacy `null`) → the existing **200** idempotent no-op, differ → new `SubmissionConflictException` → **`409 submission_conflict`** (a distinct code from the version-drift `submission_version_superseded`; `bootstrap/app.php` render closure). Batch `sync/submissions` maps it per-item. Both 409 causes converge on the same client resolution flow (only the notice copy differs). **Documented narrowing:** no server-side merge — the 409 body doesn't return the server's answers, so resolution resubmits the user's **local** copy as a fresh response; the server's copy is left for inbox reconciliation. In the guest replay path a content conflict is a defensive/multi-channel edge (queued rows are immutable) — its everyday effect is making idempotency content-aware.

The companion check — `tests/Unit` + `tests/Feature` summing exactly to the collected total — was **self-referential**, since both halves come from the same incomplete collection. The static `it(`-declaration counts were sound and stay sound; they were simply measuring a different thing from the runner. **The correct local check is the FILE COUNT, exactly as for Vitest:** `find tests -name '*Test.php' | wc -l` (330) against the distinct classes in `--list-tests` (285).

**I7b (do not re-open):** **THE GENERIC SUPER-ADMIN BYPASS IS WRONG ON `audits`, AND IT IS ALWAYS ONE LINE AWAY.** `TenantIsolation::applySuperAdminBypass('audits', ['SELECT'])` would have shipped a working platform audit viewer immediately — and handed the operator **every tenant's complete history** (every form title, every reviewer's `returned_reason`, every membership change in the deployment) in order to display a handful of platform-settings rows. **The helper's gate is a DEFAULT, NOT A CONTRACT**: it is correct only where the base shape is `nullable_global` (the tenant slice is already public there) and wrong on anything strict or append-only. `audits` therefore took a new NAMED generator, **`TenantIsolation::platformRowsBypass()`**, emitting `audits_platform_select` with `… AND tenant_id IS NULL`. **The plan said HAND-WRITE that policy; ADR-0002 §D2 says policies are generated by a reusable helper "not hand-written per table", and the user chose the generator** — the narrowing was the real requirement, hand-writing was only the means. ADR-0002 §D3 now carries the amendment. **THE POLICY NAME IS `audits_platform_select`, DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THE `audits_superadmin_%` PREFIX** the older bypass migration sweeps in its `down()`: a shared prefix lets an unrelated rollback drop this policy while its `GRANT SELECT` survives, and the page then renders **zero rows with no error** under copy saying nobody has ever performed a platform action — a plausible lie on a compliance surface. It also keeps a `pg_policies` grep for `%_superadmin_%` an honest answer to "where does the operator hold an unrestricted read". **MUTATION-VERIFIED, AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT PROVED NOTHING WHILE LOOKING LIKE IT DID.** Mutating the LIVE database is useless — `RefreshDatabase` runs `migrate:fresh` and rebuilds the correct policy underneath you, so the suite stayed green on a deliberately broken database. **The migration FILE is what must be mutated.** Done properly: swapping the generator for `applySuperAdminBypass()` reddens three `PlatformAuditRlsTest` cases including "never lets the elevated role read a TENANT-scoped audit row"; removing `withoutGlobalScope(Audit::$tenantScope)` reddens 9 of 11 `PlatformAuditReadTest` cases. **`whereNull('tenant_id')` IS NOT REDUNDANT WITH THE POLICY** and is three things at once: the ORM half of the isolation, defence in depth, and the query plan — `audits_tenant_select` has no `TO` clause so it applies to the elevated role too, Postgres OR-composes same-command permissive policies, and only a user-level leakproof `IS NULL` lets the planner keep the ordered scan on `audits_tenant_recent_idx`. "The policy already does that" is exactly how it gets deleted. **TWO LIVE 500s WERE FOUND AND FIXED, both latent since H5a purely because no UI ever called those routes:** `GET /admin/tenants/not-a-uuid` reached Postgres as `where id = 'not-a-uuid'` on a uuid column → **SQLSTATE 22P02, a 500 not a 404** (fixed with `->whereUuid('tenant')`), and `plan_id=garbage` did the same through `exists:plans,id`. **`'uuid'` ALONE DOES NOT FIX THE SECOND ONE** — Laravel short-circuits an attribute only after an *implicit* rule fails, so the rule set must be `['required','bail','uuid','exists:plans,id']`. Both mutation-verified against the real 22P02. **`EntitlementService::forget()` IS CALLED ON BOTH SIDES OF `tenantSnapshot()`, AND THIS TRACKER'S OWN STATED REASON FOR IT WAS WRONG.** It said the memo would carry one tenant's plan "into the rest of the render"; that cannot happen — inertia-laravel calls `Inertia::share()` BEFORE the controller, and `currentPlan()` early-returns on a null tenant id before it ever consults the memo. The real reason is the TEST process: the service is bound `scoped()` and **only the queue worker calls `forgetScopedInstances()`**, so one instance survives every `$this->get()`/`$this->post()` in a Pest run, and a render→mutate→render test would otherwise assert a stale plan **in the passing direction**. **EVERY FAILURE MODE ON THE DETAIL PAGE IS SILENT.** Move any read out of the adopt-context transaction and `storage_bytes` reads 0, `active_seats` reads 0, the owner reads null, the plan reads null — nothing throws. The owner assertion and the "usage reads the right tenant" assertion exist for exactly that. **`MdsModal`'s slot is `actions`; `MdsCard`'s is `footer`** — using `#footer` on a modal renders the confirm buttons NOWHERE, silently, and a Vitest case is what caught it. **THE ADMIN NAV OVERFLOWS BELOW ~900px AND ALWAYS DID.** `.admin__bar` is a fixed-height 56px flex row and the breakpoint that reflows it was 480px; five nav links measure ~860px against a ~720px content box at 768px, and the four pre-I7b links were already ~767px. Nothing in CI can see it — `/admin/*` is excluded from the Playwright sweep because `superadmin.mfa` needs a TOTP. Breakpoint raised to 900px, and the coverage gap is now a named residual in the threat model. **`clearPlatformRows()` / `committedSuperAdmin()` MOVED FROM `PlatformSettingsWriteTest` INTO `tests/Pest.php`** — Pest loads every file into one process, so a second declaration is a fatal redeclare. **THE FIXTURE PURGE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: audits → tenants → users.** `audits.tenant_id` is `nullOnDelete`, so deleting a fixture tenant first does not delete its audit rows — it PROMOTES them into permanent platform rows the viewer under test then displays, this run and every run after. The same mechanism is a real product consequence: hard-deleting a tenant moves its whole history onto `/admin/audit-log` (now recorded in data-dictionary §13 and the threat model). **TENANT-DETAIL TESTS USE ORDINARY FACTORIES, NOT I7a's COMMITTED FIXTURES** — nothing on that page elevates, so the committed apparatus would be pure cost, and registering `purgeCommittedFeedbackFixtures()` there would sweep `slug LIKE 'console-%'` across unrelated suites. **⚠️ LOCAL PHPSTAN ON THIS MACHINE IS BLIND TO ELOQUENT MODEL PROPERTIES AND REPORTS ~64 PHANTOM ERRORS; CI REPORTS `[OK] No errors` ON THE SAME TREE** — same larastan v3.10.0, same PHP 8.4, vendor synced to `composer.lock`. Every one is a `property.notFound` on a model or an `unresolvableType` downstream of one; confirmed with a two-method probe where the method touching a model property errored and the identical method without one did not. **Do not chase them and do not "fix" code to satisfy them — but do NOT trust a green local run either, and this is the half that cost real time.** The blindness cuts BOTH ways: an unresolvable model type degrades to `mixed`, and `mixed` SILENCES downstream errors. NO_TENANT_SENTINEL>` — to every Eloquent query, independently of RLS. An UPDATE bypass would write `tenant_id = NULL` and hide the operator's handling from exactly the people entitled to see it. **`attachments` HAS NO BYPASS AT ALL, DELIBERATELY** — the console reads a screenshot by adopting the report's tenant context; a bypass there would hand the operator every respondent file and every OCR scan in the deployment in order to display one image. `FeedbackRlsTest` asserts both absences by querying `pg_policies`, so a later "for symmetry" addition fails there first. **THE AUDIT ALIAS IS THE PLURAL `feedback_reports`** — matching `AuditRedactor::PII` and `AuditableTypes::LABELS`, unlike the singular `submission`/`attachment`. It would also diverge `localhost` from `127.0.0.1` locally, since both sit in `central_domains` while only one is `central_domain`. `RequirePlatformHost` already draws exactly the right line, so `PlatformLandingController` branches on `PlatformHost::subdomainLabel()`/`tenantFor()` **inside** the existing route; `PlatformLandingTest`'s last case asserts "404, **and specifically not a redirect**" so the change fails loudly rather than quietly. **`$request->user()` IS SAFE THERE WITH NO TENANT GUC** and this looks wrong next to `OpenTenantRegistrationTest`, which records that a per-tenant *settings* question in that state fails closed and silently: identity is the exception, because `config/auth.php`'s `users` provider is **`rls_aware`** and resolves on `pgsql_auth` precisely so login/registration/reset work against the fail-closed join-shape policy. **Do not add `EstablishTenantDatabaseContext` to that route.** The closure became a controller because a route **closure makes `route:cache` throw**. **`Welcome.vue` STAYS SELF-LAID-OUT** — `app.ts` excludes it by name, DSR §3.0's two shells do not fit a guest hero (`AuthLayout` is ~400px), and it is logged as **exceptions-log #8**; it is the first and only consumer of `--mds-type-display` / `--mds-space-16` / `--mds-space-24`, which the DSR has reserved for this class of surface since G11. Its `registrationOpen` prop must stay: without it the front door offers a button `GateRegistration` 404s. **`DatabaseSeeder`'s `WithoutModelEvents` MUST NOT COME BACK** — it wraps the whole run and every `->call()`ed child in `Model::withoutEvents()`, killing `HasUuidv7::creating` (the uuid PK; `users.id` has no DB default) and `BelongsToTenant::creating` (`tenant_id`, without which strict RLS refuses the row). There are **zero Observer classes in this repository**, so it protected nothing and broke `migrate:fresh --seed` for months, unseen because **nothing had ever executed that file**; `DatabaseSeederSmokeTest` is now the thing that would catch it. **`DemoSeeder` MUST NEVER WRITE INTO `acme`** — `E2eSeederIdempotencyTest` pins that fixture's counts exactly, and coupling a convenience fixture to a merge-blocking gate is how an unrelated PR starts failing. **THE AUDIT TAIL'S BACK-DATING IS AN INSERT, NOT AN UPDATE, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE PERMISSION** — `audits` is `append_only` (strict SELECT + strict INSERT, **no UPDATE/DELETE policy at all**), so `forceFill(...)->saveQuietly()` is structurally impossible there while supplying `created_at` on the INSERT is fine. **Do not add an `occurredAt` parameter to `AuditLogger`**; `E2eSeeder.php:1096-1099` forbids it and this did not need it. `redacted_fields` on those rows is **produced by `AuditRedactor`**, never authored — the same discipline `AnswerIndexProjector` enforces for the index, and for the same reason: a hand-written redaction list is a fiction the viewer then renders as fact. **THE REVIEWER'S GRANT SET DELIBERATELY EXCLUDES `Patient Intake`** — it carries ~420 of the ~520 rows, so granting it made the reviewer see 446 where an Owner sees 497, which is correct and completely invisible;
