Four locked forks: **`webhook_deliveries` EXTENDED** into the shared outbound ledger (nullable owner FKs + an XOR CHECK + two PARTIAL uniques), not a second table; **fixed Block Kit message** (templating waits for H6a — `SlackMessageFormatter` is the seam); **hand-rolled `ConnectorProvider` adapter**, no Socialite; **ADR-0009**. The load-bearing constraint: **`SESSION_DOMAIN` is null ⇒ host-only cookie**, so the central-domain callback has neither session nor tenant (and a context-less INSERT under FORCE RLS writes **zero rows without erroring**) — identity crosses the boundary in a **signed, domain-separated, provider-bound HMAC `state`** verified **pre-RLS**, the return host comes from the **`domains` table** (never echoed), and the outcome is a **query param, not a flash**. Tokens are `encrypted`-cast **`text`**, `$hidden`, **never returned in any form, not even masked**. **Two Slack gotchas for H15b/H16:** it reports failure with **HTTP 200 + `{"ok":false}`**, and its bot tokens **don't expire** by default (so the refresh sweep skips them). Full detail in the H15a + H1g (as-built) bullets under Current Status + ADR-0009 §D1–§D10.

**H14 (do not re-open):** the webhook mgmt UI is a **session-authed web layer** (`Tenant\WebhookController` + `WebhookEndpointPresenter` + `routes/tenant.php`) delegating to the **existing** `WebhookEndpointService`/`WebhookTester` — NOT the bearer `/api/v1/webhooks` surface (a session carries no token) → no `/api/v1`/migration/OpenAPI change. One-shot plaintext secret (create/rotate) + the synchronous test.ping result both ride the shared `flash` prop bridge (`newSecret`/`testResult`), read once by their modals. Sub-Starter tiers HIDE the surface (nav gated on `manageWebhooks` AND `entitlements.features.webhooks`; the route's `feature:webhooks` bounces a direct visit with a toast). Delivery log is OFFSET-paginated (MdsPagination needs page counts). **Gates already verified locally VIA THE DOCKER CONTAINERS** (`docker exec …-app-1 … vendor/bin/pest` for Pest, `…-node-1 npx vitest run` / `npm run build` for frontend — the host CLI lacks `pdo_pgsql` + the `rolldown` win32 binding): Pint, PHPStan L8 (0 on touched), controller-gate/migration-lint/job-payload-lint, vue-tsc (both), **Pest 19/19 (webhook files), Vitest 489/490 (1 pre-existing timeout flake), Vite build** — all green. **Storybook axe + Playwright responsive-axe ran for the first time in CI and were GREEN — 6/6 on the first run, no red cycle** (PR #69 `c5be98f`). **New standing lesson (the H12b toolbar-overflow lesson generalized):** the 375px no-horizontal-overflow gate is tripped by ANY non-wrapping flex row of actions, not just the builder toolbar — the shell's shared `.page-header__actions` had `display:flex` with no `flex-wrap`, and the H14 detail page puts FIVE buttons in that slot. Fixed pre-emptively (`flex-wrap: wrap` in `PageHeader.vue`, now shared by every page) together with the list's URL cell (`max-width: min(22rem, 100%)` — a fixed `22rem` = 352px exceeds the ~343px a 375px viewport gives the DataTable's card-mode cell). **Audit any new multi-button action slot / fixed `max-width` against the 375px budget BEFORE pushing.**

**H13a+H13b design (do not re-open):** monthly `webhook_deliveries` quota = HARD cap (over → `dead_lettered` `[quota_exceeded]`, not sent); subscribable events = all four `DomainEventType` cases (REUSED, no `WebhookEventType`); `secret`/`secret_previous` are `text` (encrypted-cast overflows varchar 255); retry ladder lives in `next_retry_at` swept by `SweepWebhookRetriesJob` (NOT `$tries`/`backoff()`); SSRF is one `OutboundUrlGuard` at BOTH save + every delivery; endpoint cap = gauge `UsageMetric::WebhookEndpointsCount` (Starter 3 / Pro 10). **H13b:** test.ping = SYNCHRONOUS inline (`WebhookTester`, no delivery row, `test.ping` never in the DB `event_type` column); redeliver = EXEMPT from re-metering (`DeliverWebhookJob` scalar `skipMeter`, re-runs SSRF, 404 cross-endpoint / 409 not-active); payload archival = OVERSIZED-AT-CREATION over `payload_archive_threshold_bytes` (`WebhookPayloadArchive` → `payload_attachment_id` seam + `webhook_delivery` morph alias, read back before signing); dual-secret rotation signs with BOTH via `WebhookSigner::signatureHeaderFor` during the `secret_rotation_grace_seconds` window; auto-disable = queued `WebhookAutoDisabledNotification` to the tenant owner on the breaker-trip edge. **CI GOTCHA (cost H13a a red PR run):** local openapi verification runs only the drift-diff, NOT `redocly lint` — every new controller method that becomes an operation MUST carry a PHPDoc first line (Scramble → operation `summary`; the `operation-summary` rule fails without it). `gh` is NOT pre-authed — export `GH_TOKEN` from `git credential fill` first (see Env notes). PHPStan: run `phpstan analyse --memory-limit=2G` locally (128M OOMs); the ~76 full-analyse errors are the known local baseline (CI is clean), so only ensure ZERO in touched files. **Full detail in the H13a + H13b (as-built) bullets under Current Status.**

**H5a…H11 + H12a are MERGED** (PR #54–63; all CI-green) — **the entitlement track, the server-side draft substrate (H9→a/b), the save-and-resume UX (H10), the basic dashboard KPIs (H11), AND the scheduled-forms backend (H12a) are on `main`.** **H12a is MERGED** (PR #63 `a07beae`; Pest 1271, all gates green) and **H12b (scheduled-forms UI) is MERGED** (PR #64 `2278f2d`, all 6 CI green) — **next = H13a.** (H12b CI gotcha for H13a: adding a builder toolbar button overflowed the non-wrapping `.builder__actions` at narrow viewports / large personalization fonts, which cascaded into axe color-contrast flags as buttons spilled off the light toolbar — fixed with `flex-wrap`; watch the responsive-overflow gate whenever you add a toolbar control.) **H12b design (do not re-open):** the builder config is a **modal from a "Schedule" toolbar button** (Inertia `useForm().patch` for inline 422s); the request **interprets the naive wall-clock in the chosen tz then stores UTC** (Eloquent drops a non-UTC offset otherwise); the guest **acceptance gate is fresh-load only — the resume path is never gated** (H12a grace window); **offline fail-closed is scoped to scheduled/capped forms** (unscheduled forms keep the G8b outbox); the encode path is **banner + disabled submit** (form stays visible); both presenters share **`FormScheduleView`** so the wire shape can't drift. **New standing lesson from H2 — the framework is also "reality", not just migrations.** The existing lesson says *§-numbered docs describe intent; migrations and code describe reality*. H2 extends it: **an ADR's claims about a FRAMEWORK API are intent too.** Five of ADR-0007's thirteen sub-decisions were wrong against the installed version — not vaguely, but in ways that would have shipped a leak (`JobProcessed` misses the failure path), a self-inflicted outage (`$tries` inverting the fairness it sits next to; the §D13 enum-vs-string comparison releasing every job on the platform), or a fatal error (`$queue` as a property). The ADR anticipated this at `:178` and said so; **the discipline that worked was reading `vendor/` for every API the plan leaned on, and then proving each correction by mutation rather than by argument.** Related, cheap, and worth repeating: `sed -i` with a `$` anchor silently no-ops on this repo's CRLF files — a mutation that appears to apply but doesn't will quietly tell you a test is stronger than it is. Verify the mutant landed before trusting the red.

**Standing lesson reinforced by H1a — the third instance:** §-numbered docs describe *intent*; migrations and code describe *reality*. Verification refuted **six** `file:line` citations in an otherwise-correct plan, plus two H-map claims that would have written new errors into the corpus (the "27 permissions" correction — the doc already says 28 — and an 8-item PRD roadmap row that does not exist). Before G11 it was the `accent` column that "already existed" and didn't. **Grep every claim of the form "X exists" before writing it into a document**, and prefer characterising the *absence* precisely ("no first-party outbound HTTP call site") over the sweeping version ("no guzzle"), which was false.

**CI took two follow-up fixes, both harness-shaped and both predicted as the top risks:**
1. `frontend` — `token-references.test.ts` threw `ERR_INVALID_URL_SCHEME` on CI while passing locally. The suite runs under `environment: 'happy-dom'`, whose DOM `URL` global shadows Node's, and resolving a five-level **directory** URL (trailing slash) through it does not preserve the `file:` scheme. Its sibling suites use the identical `import.meta.url` pattern and pass because they resolve concrete **file** paths. Fixed with `process.cwd()` (Vitest's cwd is its config's directory = repo root). **New standing gotcha: prefer `process.cwd()` over `import.meta.url` arithmetic in Vitest suites that need the repo root.**
2. `tests` — the new guest-shell test threw `Vite manifest not found`. It is the only test in `GuestRuntimeTest` that renders the SHELL rather than hitting a JSON endpoint, so the only one evaluating `@vite`; the Pest job builds no assets. It passed locally purely because assets happened to be built. Fixed with `withoutVite()` (the existing convention). **Reproduced deliberately by moving `public/build/manifest.json` aside — worth doing for any test that renders a blade view.**

The two jobs feared most (`design-system-a11y` for story attribute leakage, `e2e` for the font-loading race and 375×extra_large reflow) **passed on the first run** — the mitigations held.

True two-session contention is not exercised: `RefreshDatabase` wraps each test in an uncommitted transaction so a second connection cannot see the fixtures, and the suite has no committing-Feature-test precedent. Adding one means a file without `RefreshDatabase` plus manual cleanup — worth doing if this area changes again.

**Env notes:** local Postgres runs on `postgis/postgis:17-3.5` (first-time pull needs `docker compose down -v && docker compose up -d` for the PostGIS init SQL). **`gh` CLI is NOT pre-authed in the shell** — read its token from the git credential helper: `export GH_TOKEN="$(printf 'protocol=https\nhost=github.com\n\n' | git credential fill 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^password=//p')"` before any `gh` command. **That token has only `gist`/`repo`/`workflow` scopes**, so any `gh` subcommand that goes through GraphQL and touches org fields fails — `gh pr edit` is the one that bites (it asks for `login`/`name`/`slug` and errors with "requires one of the following scopes: ['read:org']"). Use the REST path instead: `gh api -X PATCH repos/OWNER/REPO/pulls/N -F body=@file`. `gh pr create`, `gh pr merge`, `gh pr checks` and `gh pr view` are all fine.

## Verification loop (per increment)

`docker compose up -d` → `docker compose exec app php artisan migrate:fresh --force` → **`docker compose exec app php -d memory_limit=3G vendor/bin/pest`** (real Postgres — see the memory note below; the bare `php artisan test` no longer reaches the end of the suite) → `composer run quality` + `npm run type-check` on the host → push branch → `gh pr create` → CI green (6 jobs) → `gh pr merge --squash`. `gh` CLI authed via `GH_TOKEN`. Local Docker runs ~3× slower than CI (WSL2 volume I/O), not a code issue.

**⚠️ NEVER TWO PEST PROCESSES AT ONCE — RE-LEARNED THE HARD WAY IN I7a.** A filtered run started while the full suite was still going dropped the schema under it (`relation "permissions" does not exist`, mid-run, on `meridian_testing`) and produced **five bogus failures** that looked exactly like real ones. Cost: one wasted 17-minute run. Related: **`vendor/bin/pest`'s exit code cannot be trusted** — it returned 0 alongside `Tests: 5 failed`. Read the summary line, never `$?`.

**⚠️ THE FULL LOCAL SUITE NOW OOMs, AND IT IS A CONTAINER CONFIG DIVERGENCE, NOT A CODE DEFECT (found I7a).** `php artisan test` dies at **exactly 981 tests** with `Allowed memory size of 134217728 bytes exhausted` inside `RouteFileRegistrar::require`. The container loads **no php.ini at all** (`Loaded Configuration File => (none)`) so PHP's built-in `memory_limit = 128M` applies, while CI's `shivammathur/setup-php` defaults CLI memory to **unlimited** — which is why CI runs the same suite to completion and why this was invisible until the suite grew past the line. **`php -d memory_limit=…` in front of `artisan test` does NOT work**: `artisan test` re-execs PHP for the Pest subprocess and the flag is lost. Invoke **`vendor/bin/pest` directly** with the flag. Same environment class as the PHPStan OOM below, and it deserves the same treatment: fix the invocation, do not chase the "failure".

## Gotchas / standing lessons

- **A COMMITTED test fixture is global state, and it needs a purge marker the cleanup can MATCH (I7a, and again — expensively — in I11a).** Any fixture written on `pgsql_privileged` to be visible from `pgsql_superadmin` escapes RefreshDatabase's rollback, and `migrate:fresh` runs once per process, so the only thing that removes it is a purge keyed on a naming marker. A slug outside that marker leaks for the whole run. It cost nine tests in I7a and twelve in I11a, both times in suites with no connection to the change: the seeder smoke tests pin the exact `tenants.slug` list, and the sweep/reaper/rollup suites drain a FIXED number of queued jobs on the assumption their own tenant is the only active one, so a second tenant makes the drain consume the stranger's child and the test's own tenant is never swept. `committedPlatformTenant()` now THROWS on a slug outside `platform-audit-`, with `tests/Unit/CommittedFixtureMarkerTest.php` as the mutation guard — **mint new committed fixtures the same way, marker-first**.
- **Read the failure output before bisecting — an assertion that prints a diff of GLOBAL STATE has already done the bisect for you (I11a).** #119 burned a session on three disproved hypotheses and a queued `git revert` bisect while `DatabaseSeederSmokeTest`'s own diff was naming the leaked tenant by slug in the log. Symptom distance is not causal distance: "the sweep did nothing" and "an unexpected row exists" were the same bug.
- **NEVER assert a hypothesis as a measurement in a docblock (I11a).** A comment claiming a change "COST TWELVE FAILURES" was written before the next CI run disproved it, and it then sat in the tree pointing every future reader at an innocent method. If it was not measured, say it was not — a wrong attribution is more expensive than no note.
- **A `setTestNow()` reset written as the last STATEMENT of a test body only runs while that test PASSES.** Use `$this->travelTo()`, which restores in `tearDown` on every exit path. (Laravel's `TestCase::tearDown()` also resets test-now, so this is about the code reading as a leak, not being one.)
- **`builder-axe.spec.ts` carried its OWN weaker `forceTheme`, and that was a real latent race — fixed H21d1.** The shared helper in `tests/e2e/support/axe.ts` calls `page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' })` FIRST, which collapses the design system's durations to 1ms centrally (`theme-overrides.css` §2.8) so axe cannot sample an element mid theme-flip. `builder-axe` had a local copy that skipped that step. The symptom is unmistakable once you know it: a `color`-transitioned label inside a container whose `background-color` is NOT transitioned reads as the **light** foreground on the **dark** surface — H21d1's `Structure ⇄ Logic` label measured **1.82:1** on CI while the same node settles at **6.96:1**. It presents as a serious `color-contrast` violation in a component that is fine. **If a dark-mode contrast failure names a foreground colour that belongs to the LIGHT palette, it is a transition race, not a palette defect** — check that the spec uses the shared `forceTheme`.
- **A "known flake" can be hiding a real failure — re-run it in isolation before waving it through (found H21d1).** `packages/design-system/src/theme/__tests__/token-references.test.ts` has failed as a 5s timeout in the FULL Vitest run since H21b and is recorded here as a flake. In H21d1 the isolated re-run reported a genuinely undefined `--mds-type-body-font-size` in new CSS — and a dangling token with no fallback makes the whole declaration invalid at computed-value time, so the element scales by *inheritance* under `[data-font-size]` rather than by its type role. Cost of the check: one `npx vitest run <that file>`. **Always run it.**
- **New copy must be checked against the DARK palette specifically (found H21d1).** `--mds-color-danger-text` resolves to `danger-300` in dark, which is **4.22:1** on `bg-surface` at 13px — a real `color-contrast` violation that only the dark axe scan sees. The `status-*-fg` family (`--mds-color-status-danger-fg` / `-warning-fg`) is the on-surface pair, at 8.43:1 light and 6.39:1 dark. When adding status text on a surface, reach for `status-*-fg`.
- **~~`builder-axe` dark fails LOCALLY on `main` too — do not chase it~~ — THAT DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG, and H21d1 found the real cause.** The note recorded a `color-contrast` failure on `.mds-button--secondary`/`--primary` in dark at all three viewports, reproduced it on `main`, ruled out stale tokens and axe drift, and concluded it was "a local-environment divergence in the rendered dark palette" to be distrusted. It was neither local nor a divergence. **Two real defects were stacked on top of each other.** **(1) A genuine WCAG 1.4.3 failure in the shared dark palette:** `--mds-color-action-primary-bg-hover` was `primary-400` (**3.96:1** against the white `text-on-primary`) and `-bg-active` was `primary-300` (**2.52:1**) — the dark theme LIGHTENED the fill on hover, which is the opposite of what a white-on-fill button needs and the opposite of what the light theme does. The teal accent had carried per-token verification in a comment since G11; the default accent never did. Both now darken (`primary-600` 9.14:1, `primary-700` 13.00:1) and a **test** guards it (`theme-overrides.test.ts`), because a comment is not a guard. **(2) A transition race in the harness:** `builder-axe.spec.ts` carried its own `forceTheme` that skipped the shared helper's `emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' })`, so axe sampled elements mid theme-flip — which is why the failure looked intermittent and viewport-dependent, and why CI passed while local did not. With both fixed, `builder-axe` is **10/10 locally in dark**. **The lesson to carry is the opposite of the one that was written down: a reproducible local a11y failure is evidence, not noise.** Reproducing it on `main` proves it is not the branch's — it does NOT prove it is not real.
- **~~Never run Pest and Playwright at the same time — they share one database.~~ — THE MECHANISM IN THAT DIAGNOSIS IS WRONG, corrected in I6, and the correction matters because it changes what you have to avoid.** They do **not** share a database. `phpunit.xml:42` has pinned `DB_DATABASE=meridian_testing` since the Phase-0 walking skeleton, `DB_DATABASE` is **not** set as a container environment variable (so nothing can pre-empt the pin), and Playwright serves the app from `.env` on `meridian`. Verified directly in I6: the full 1007-second suite ran to completion against `meridian_testing` — 8 live connections to it throughout — while the dev database kept its 534 seeded submissions untouched. **So `php artisan test` is safe to run while you are using the app.** What is *not* safe, and is the likeliest real cause of the two discarded runs this note was written for: **`migrate:fresh` run by hand**, which targets `.env` and therefore does wipe the dev database out from under a live e2e run; and **Playwright's own global setup**, which seeds `E2eSeeder` into `meridian` and will replace whatever demo data you were looking at. Both still deserve the caution — just not the one the note gave. Reseed afterwards with `php artisan db:seed --class="Database\Seeders\E2eSeeder"` for Playwright, or `migrate:fresh --seed` to get the I6 demo fixture back; **`migrate:fresh --seed` does NOT include the e2e fixture**, so a Playwright run straight after it fails at global-setup's login.
- **Playwright has no `.bin` shim on this host** (the documented `--no-bin-links` consequence) — invoke it as `node node_modules/@playwright/test/cli.js test`, with `E2E_BASE_URL=http://acme.localhost:8080` to reuse the running docker stack.
- **phpstan local OOM** — `composer run quality`'s phpstan OOMs its parallel workers at 128M locally → phantom "undefined property"/relation-nullability errors. CI's Larastan (`disableMigrationScan: false`) scans `database/migrations`, resolves every column → 0 errors → green is the source of truth. For possibly-null relation chains prefer `data_get($m, 'rel.attr')` over `?->`.
- **PHP 8.3** removed `${var}` string interpolation → single-quote grammar snippets in tests (don't let `${...}` interpolate).
- **Windows npm** — a nested design-system esbuild-bin file-lock breaks `npm install <pkg>` → use `--no-bin-links` locally (CI's Linux `npm ci` relinks fine). Consequence (seen in G9b): `node_modules/@rolldown` holds only Linux bindings and `--no-bin-links` leaves no `vitest`/`vite` shim → **`npm run build` and `npx vitest` cannot run on the Windows host** (rolldown `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, "'vitest' is not recognized"). **`vue-tsc` DOES run** (no native binding), so treat it as the local frontend gate; build + Vitest are CI-only.
- **IndexedDB can't clone Vue proxies (G8b)** — `structuredClone` (every IndexedDB write) throws `DataCloneError` on a reactive Proxy, in real browsers too. Always `plainClone()` (JSON round-trip, `lib/db.ts`) an answer map before a Dexie `put`. Related: happy-dom `Blob`s don't survive `fake-indexeddb`'s `structuredClone` round-trip (assert metadata, not the reconstituted Blob); and `vite-plugin-pwa` `injectManifest` emits an import-free ES bundle that registers fine as a **classic** worker (no `{type:'module'}`).
- **Vitest + repo-root paths (G11)** — suites run under `environment: 'happy-dom'`, whose DOM `URL` global shadows Node's. `fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../../../', import.meta.url))` resolves fine locally but throws `ERR_INVALID_URL_SCHEME` on CI when the target is a **directory** (trailing slash); concrete **file** paths are unaffected, which is why sibling suites using the same pattern pass. Use **`process.cwd()`** for the repo root — Vitest's cwd is its config file's directory.
- **Any Pest test that renders a blade view needs `withoutVite()` (G11)** — the Pest CI job builds no assets, so `@vite` throws `Vite manifest not found`. It passes locally whenever `public/build` happens to exist, which makes it a silent local/CI divergence. Reproduce by moving `public/build/manifest.json` aside before running.
- **Base64url tamper tests** (was "known-flaky", FIXED in G10b2): flipping the LAST base64url char can alias to the same decoded bytes — a 32-byte HMAC is 42.7 six-bit groups, so the trailing char carries 2 padding bits. Flip the FIRST char. Both `GuestRuntimeTest` and `GuestShareTokenServiceTest::tamperSegment` now do; there is no known flaky test left.
